We are seeking a Director of Software Development to lead Language Foundations, the organization that owns Amazon's programming-languages strategy across our strategic languages (Java, Rust, Python, TypeScript, Go, C/C++, Kotlin, and Swift) and represents that strategy to the language community: the engineers who specialize in language design, compilation, and optimization, along with standards bodies and the open-source ecosystems Amazon depends on. Amazon EC2 Hardware Engineering designs and builds the servers that power Amazon Web Services. We take the silicon our partners create and design the boards, servers, and racks around it, then own the full lifecycle: new product introduction (NPI), design validation, launch, manufacturing ramp, and in-fleet sustaining engineering across compute, storage, networking, edge, and accelerator products.
We are looking for a world-class engineering leader (Director, Hardware Development) to own a server product line end to end. This is a hands-on hardware-engineering leadership role: your organization owns the hardware design, system integration, and system engineering for a product family, and is accountable for delivering it from design through volume manufacturing and into a large-scale global fleet that must run reliably for years.
This is a leadership role with exceptional surface area. The space is broad, and the depth is multilayered: you will lead multiple teams through their managers, set multi-year technical and product strategy for your product line, operate deep in the engineering when it matters, and work externally with ODMs and vendors at a detailed technical level to drive roadmaps and secure supply. You will partner with the component and firmware teams your products depend on, and with Principal and Distinguished Engineers and senior leaders across AWS. The problems are hard, the scale is among the largest in the world, and the work is visible to the most senior leaders at AWS.

• Own a server product family end to end: hardware design, system integration, and system engineering, from NPI (New Product Introduction)and design validation through launch, manufacturing ramp, and in-fleet sustaining.
• Own hardware quality and velocity for your product line, and be accountable for manufacturing yield and throughput targets and for resolving manufacturing-engineering defects.
• Lead multiple engineering teams through their managers; hire, grow, and develop managers and engineers, and scale the organization to meet an aggressive roadmap.
• Set the multi-year technical and product strategy for your product line and make long-term engineering decisions that balance innovation with reliability at scale.
• Manage strategic relationships with ODM design and manufacturing partners (domestic and overseas)
• Own fleet-reliability outcomes for your products (annualized failure rate, unsellable reduction, proactive defect remediation).
• Partner across hardware, firmware, software, operations, and supply chain, and drive external roadmaps with partner teams.

You will work on problems that do not have textbook answers and where the questions themselves may not even be known. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Trusted by thousands of women nationwide, Allara makes expert healthcare accessible by connecting patients with multidisciplinary care teams that have a deep understanding of hormonal, metabolic, and reproductive care. Allara provides ongoing support for hormonal conditions like PCOS, chronic conditions like insulin resistance, and life stages like perimenopause, helping patients see improved health outcomes https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/637f55cdd2e0aa051d497c52/68e6aa0f8fcce5c60e922219_Outcomes%20Impact%20Report%202025%20Web%20Display.pdf. As one of the fastest-growing women’s health platforms in the U.S., Allara is bridging long-overlooked gaps in healthcare for women.




THE OPPORTUNITY

Allara is hiring its first Director of Data to build the backbone of how the company collects, models, governs, and uses data. Reporting to the VP of Engineering, this is a hands-on leadership role: in your first months you will be in the pipelines yourself, cleaning up our ETL, consolidating duplicated logic, and closing gaps in our source data. Over time you will define and drive the company's longer-term data strategy, set the standards the rest of the organization builds on, and grow the data function as Allara scales. This is a player-coach role, senior enough to own strategy and still happy to get the pipelines right yourself, and the hands-on work comes first.

Location: Hybrid (NYC). We value in-person collaboration and aim for at least three days per week in our NYC office, with flexibility as needed.




YOUR IMPACT

 - Make Allara's data trustworthy, so every team can make decisions on numbers they believe.

 - Turn a fragmented, duplicated data setup into one reliable source of truth with traceable lineage.

 - Define the data strategy that lets Allara scale its use of data, from AI-assisted analysis across departments and leveraging health data to drive better outcomes.

 - Build and lead the data engineering function over time.

 - Partner with Product, Growth, Finance, Strategy, and Clinical as the owner of the shared data platform and standards.




RESPONSIBILITIES

THE 4 BIGGEST BLOCKCHAIN STRENGTHS ARE ALSO ITS WEAKNESS

 - Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

 - Decentralization leads to too many standards https://xkcd.com/927/

 - Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

 - Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.




BLOCKCHAINS ARE OPTIMIZED FOR WRITES, NOT READS. 

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases https://x.com/Tim_Roughgarden/status/1512847113599729668. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

 - Fragmented standards

 - Exponential complexity

 - No accountability for interpretation

 - Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.




ALLIUM IS BUILDING THE SYSTEM OF RECORD FOR ONCHAIN FINANCE

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

 - Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

 - Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

 - Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

 - Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.




FINANCE IS MOVING ONCHAIN

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously https://x.com/AlliumLabs/status/2019810793324482901?s=20, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability. 

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

Campfire is a next-gen core accounting platform built for modern mid-market finance teams. We’re building the future of ERP by replacing outdated systems and manual accounting processes with an AI-native platform that helps finance teams move faster and operate more efficiently.

The role

Campfire is hiring its first full-time CISO to own security, compliance and customer trust as we sell to larger enterprises.

 - Campfire is an AI-native ERP and financial automation platform. We raised a $65M Series B led by Accel and Ribbit Capital.

 - Customers trust us with their general ledger, bank details, payroll and vendor data.

 - Today, security is run by a fractional vCISO firm plus a few engineers. Deals are increasingly gated on security reviews.

 - You will turn that into an in-house program that closes deals faster and keeps us safe.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Customer security reviews and deal support

 - Answer security questionnaires, TPRMs and RFPs (SIG, CAIQ, custom) with a fast, predictable turnaround.

 - Join customer and prospect calls with CIOs and IT security teams, including implementation kickoffs.

 - Maintain a trust center and security collateral pack: policies, pentest reports, network architecture, insurance certificate.

Compliance and audits

 - Own SOC 1 and SOC 2 (Type I and II): scope, auditor management, bridge letters, and customer follow-up questions.

 - Decide and lead the path to ISO 27001, ISO 42001 and other frameworks customers ask about.

 - Run Vanta as the system of record for controls and evidence.

Privacy and contracts

 - Partner with Legal on DPAs, BAAs, GDPR transfer mechanisms (SCCs / DPF), DORA and non-US privacy laws.

 - Review security and audit-cooperation clauses in customer contracts.

 - Own data retention, export and residency answers, including new-region or GovCloud requests.

Security operations and incident response

 - Own the incident response plan, run tabletop tests, and lead response when incidents happen.

 - Own customer breach notification decisions and post-incident write-ups.

 - Own detection and email security: SIEM, EDR, email protection, identity alerting.

Identity and access

 - Own Okta (SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, SCIM), MDM and least-privilege access to production.

 - Support customer-facing SSO/SCIM setups.

Resilience and policy

 - Own BCDR plans, RTO/RPO targets, backup and restore testing.

 - Maintain information security, responsible AI and vendor management policies.

 - Run background and sanctions screening for employees and vendors.

AI security

 - Answer customer questions on our AI assistant: underlying models, prompt and response retention, logging, and opt-out.

 - Govern AI vendors and subprocessors.

ABOUT CAPE

Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data.

Instead of accepting the status quo, we decided to fix it. National security professionals, journalists, parents, and everyone in between can stay connected and have privacy.

We didn’t just build a layer on top of old tech; we built America’s most private and secure mobile carrier from the ground up. By building our own network from scratch, we are able to design and build a suite of privacy and security features that no other carrier on the planet can offer.

Today, Cape provides our secure network to consumers, businesses, and government agencies alike. We closed our Series C in March 2026, and we are scaling rapidly, with the goal of giving people back control of their most personal information.




THE TEAM

At Cape, we are the architects of a privacy-centric movement that is just getting started. We are relentless builders, constantly innovating at the edge of what's possible in telecommunications. We operate on a foundation of high trust and high expectations. Our structure is flat, and collaboration matters more than hierarchy. As a member of our team, you will collaborate with world-class engineers, architects, and visionaries, and work across organizational lines to solve "impossible" problems and deliver mission-critical results for our users every single day.




THE ROLE

The CISO is our chief protector. Our infrastructure, threat model, and customer expectations are more complex than a typical mobile carrier or a typical software company. Your challenge is to enable rapid product innovation without compromising on our goal to be the most secure commercial mobile network on the planet. You'll own the strategy and execution of security across our network, products, and corporate systems and work as a partner to Engineering and the executive team.

This is a build-and-defend role, not a maintain-the-status-quo role. You will immediately take ownership of a highly technical, responsive, and ambitious security, IT, and compliance org. Your mandate is to resource, mature, and scale this team to stay ahead of threats and enable Cape’s rapid growth.This role is based out of our NYC or DC office and reports to our founder and CEO John Doyle.






WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

Charge Robotics is a Series A startup building robots that build solar farms.

Demand for new solar projects is booming (one-fifth of all the solar that exists in the US was installed last year!), but today’s construction companies can’t keep up due to limited labor resources.

We thought this was insane, so we developed robots to directly address this bottleneck and speed up the world’s transition to renewables. We’ve shipped our first commercial system already, and are in the process of scaling up our operations to meet our massive demand.

Charge is a fast-moving company, which means constant opportunities for learning and growth. You’ll have a large impact on the direction of our company and our product, which will be reflected in significant equity compensation. And you get to work with 🤖 giant robots 🤖.

If you are excited to work on interesting technical problems with direct climate impact, you’re going to fit right in at Charge Robotics.

ABOUT THE COMPANY

At Covera Health, we're on a mission to improve healthcare by making every diagnosis more accurate.

Every year, millions of patients receive imaging that shapes life changing medical decisions. Yet too often, important findings are missed, patients struggle to access high quality imaging, and the healthcare system treats radiology like a commodity instead of one of the most critical moments in a patient's care journey.

We're changing that.

Covera combines clinical expertise, advanced AI, and one of the industry's largest radiology quality datasets to help detect disease earlier, improve diagnostic accuracy, and give clinicians greater confidence in every decision they make. Better diagnoses lead to better treatment, fewer unnecessary procedures, lower healthcare costs, and, most importantly, better outcomes for patients.

In 2026, Covera and Medmo came together to create the first platform designed to support the entire radiology journey. From helping patients find and schedule high quality imaging, to coordinating care, to ensuring the accuracy of every diagnosis, we're building a connected experience that simply hasn't existed before.

Backed by Insight Partners, our platform supports nearly 6 million people across Fortune 10 and Fortune 100 employers, three of the five largest national health plans, and thousands of value based primary care physicians.

This is an exciting moment to join Covera. We're building technology that is helping detect serious conditions earlier, improving the quality of care for millions of patients, and redefining what healthcare can be. If you're excited by meaningful work, ambitious teammates, and the opportunity to help save lives through better healthcare, we'd love to meet you.

Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure

 

Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system.

 

Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You will own Crux's relationships with the governments, communities, and public audiences that decide where and how fast Crux can build. Data centers today earn their permits, tax agreements, and utility approvals in rooms full of neighbors, county commissioners, and school boards, and increasingly in state legislatures, public utility commissions, and the press, and schedule risk concentrates there. Your job is to make Crux the developer that communities and governments say yes to, and to keep that yes durable through a multi-year build. You will build this function from zero: the government affairs strategy, the community engagement playbook, the community investment program, the corporate communications rhythm, and the relationships at every level of government and at every site in the pipeline. The role works hand-in-hand with site selection, entitlements, energy, construction, operations, and executive leadership.

 - Lead Crux's government affairs strategy at the local, state, and federal levels: build relationships with elected officials, agency and regulatory staff, and economic development agencies, and track and shape the policy issues that affect data center development, including energy and interconnection, water, tax incentives, and permitting.

 - Build and maintain relationships with the stakeholders who decide our projects' fate, including county and municipal officials, planning and zoning staff, utilities, school districts, business organizations, and community non-profits, in every market Crux enters.

 - Serve as Crux's external affairs lead and spokesperson, representing the company with policymakers, trade associations, industry coalitions, and the media, and advise executive leadership on emerging political, regulatory, and reputational issues.

 - Own the company-level communications narrative and manage the PR agency relationship: set priorities, direct agency work, and coordinate closely with executive leadership, legal, and Blackstone/Google partner teams on major company updates such as financings, partnerships, site announcements, and leadership news, so that Crux speaks with one consistent voice.

At Gallatin, we are rebuilding logistics infrastructure for the national security missions of the United States and allied partners. We build AI systems that determine how logistics decisions are made, not just how they're executed. From factory to foxhole, we operate at the layer where data becomes decisions, and decisions make the advantage.

It’s ideal for someone who has moved fluidly between the operational military world and the commercial defense tech industry.

You’ll be the primary technical authority for customers and program offices, translating complex mission requirements into secure, scalable architectures and then rolling up your sleeves to make sure they get built and delivered. You’re as comfortable in a briefing room with senior government stakeholders as you are in a terminal troubleshooting a production system.

You’ll lead pre-sales engineers who shape solutions and help win work, as well as post-sales forward deployed engineers who deploy, operate, and scale those solutions at customer sites. You’ll define how the team is organized, how work moves from pursuit to delivery, and how the function scales as our customer base grows.

Team Leadership & Org Building

HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




FORWARD DEPLOYED AT HADRIAN

We embed Forward Deployed teams on Hadrian’s largest, most critical programs with the U.S. Government, the Armed Forces, and major defense primes. The Forward Deployed team works alongside the Program team from scoping to execution.

Forward Deployed bends our product to fulfill customer needs. Sometimes that involves extending Opus, Hadrian’s AI-driven manufacturing autonomy platform, other times it involves taking a new product zero to one to make a program successful. Everything the Forward Deployed team learns working at the edge with our customers is fed back to our platform teams to improve Hadrian’s product for all customers.

Recent projects have included standing up Factories-as-a-Service for the Armed Forces and multiple primes, extending Opus into new manufacturing domains such as energetics, and taking a product that was built for a single program into a $B+ product line.

 

The Role

As Director, you lead the Forward Deployed team on one or more programs and own its technical outcomes. You’ll get to run the technical side of a program larger than most startups ever get, working directly with the government, customer’s, and Hadrian’s leadership.

The team is early and scope is rapidly growing with Hadrian. Directors will help scale the Forward Deployed team itself and be the tip of the spear on multi-billion-dollar programs:

 - Own the technical roadmap and delivery. Take the program from the first ambiguous conversation to running in production, decide what Opus covers, what gets built, and what we say no to, and hold the team to a very high execution bar. The program hits rate, quality, schedule, and cost in part because the software and systems behind it work; you own that part.

 - Bring program learnings on platform teams. Share program learnings at Hadrian to improve

The Role:
Much of the technical data behind US defense systems is decades old: scanned paper, hand-marked prints, and drawings that were never turned into 3D models. Hadrian is building a team to turn that data into modern, manufacturing-ready models and drawings. Customers can then keep their systems running, and those parts can be quoted, made at Hadrian, or procured.

The team supports multiple defense programs that need this work now. The first priority is a large, multi-year technical data migration for a defense customer. The team works alongside Hadrian's software to convert each technical data package and confirm it is right before it goes to the customer.

As Director, you build and run that operation, growing it from a small founding team into a large organization. You report to the Senior Director of Central Quality and NPI.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build the operating model for each program, starting with the migration: the standard workflow, the training, and the quality controls that confirm each package matches its source data before it goes to the customer.

 - Work with the software team so the process and the automation tools improve together, and the manual effort per package keeps falling.

 - Plan and run the hiring ramp: sourcing, location, training, and retention.

 - Balance capacity across programs, track throughput and quality against each program's schedule, and fix the bottleneck.

 - Hire and develop the leaders who run the team day to day.

 - Meet each program's data-handling rules while keeping the quality call.

   - Throughput. Technical data packages delivered each month against each program's plan.

WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey is building AI-native software for professional services. Our customers trust us with some of the world's most sensitive information, making security fundamental to everything we build. As a leader on our Product Security team, you'll help embed security into our engineering organization, enabling teams to build quickly and securely as we scale.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Product Security, you'll help shape our product security roadmap and lead a team of engineers in delivering it. Your team will own defined areas of Harvey's production surface, working closely with product and platform engineers to shape architecture, influence design decisions, and build security tooling. You'll combine people leadership with sound technical judgment to protect our customers and make secure development easier across Harvey.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

You'll partner directly with our Senior Director of Product Security to translate the broader security strategy into focused priorities and measurable outcomes for your team. You'll hire, develop, and lead Product Security Engineers, establishing clear ownership and helping them become trusted partners to their engineering counterparts. Working closely with Engineering, Product, Infrastructure, and Security, you'll align security investments with business priorities and the technical realities of our platform.

Day to day, you'll own your team's planning, prioritization, and delivery. You'll provide technical direction on architecture reviews, threat modeling, and remediation, helping engineers navigate complex security tradeoffs. About Helion

We are a fusion power company based in Everett, WA, with the mission to build the world's first fusion power plant, enabling a future with unlimited clean electricity. Our vision is a world with clean, reliable, and affordable energy for everyone.

Since Helion's founding in 2013, we have raised $1.5 billion from long-time investors such as Sam Altman, Mithril, and Capricorn Investment Group as well as new investors including Thrive Capital, LightSpeed Venture Capital, SoftBank, and others to propel us forward. Our current prototype, Polaris, has reached record-breaking plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius (13 keV). Helion is continuing to iterate and on the path to the world's first fusion power plant, Orion.

This is a pivotal time to join Helion. You will tackle real-world challenges with a team that prizes urgency, rigor, ownership, and a commitment to delivering hard truths – values essential to achieving what no one has before. Together, we will change the future of energy, because the world can't wait.


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Every Helion fusion pulse runs current through semiconductor switches operated well beyond commercial ratings. Our next generation of fusion machines requires devices designed for our circuits rather than adapted to them, gated devices integrated as multi-die modules, and packaging that survives repetitive high-energy pulsing for power plant-scale lifetimes. You will lead the team that delivers these, from device physics through a development-scale fabrication capability to pilot module assembly and test, and you will carry it into high-volume production with external fabrication partners. Your team’s work will help determine how reliably Helion’s power plants operate, how frequently they can pulse, and how effectively we can manufacture and deploy future plants.




WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

 - Own Helion’s semiconductor roadmap, working with technical leadership to define device requirements, make build-versus-buy decisions, and deliver the capabilities needed for successive generations of fusion machines

 - Build and lead a focused, multi-disciplinary team of semiconductor scientists, device R&D engineers, technicians, and a technical project manager

 - Stand up a development-scale device fabrication, characterization and reliability capability, and own the tooling, process, and facility decisions behind it

 - Direct in-house device design, including alternative device topologies optimized for Helion's pulsed-power circuits

 - Drive novel packaging and integration: multi-die packages for gated devices used in series, deeply integrated thermal management for repetitive operation, and the reliability program that qualifies them

 - Establish and lead partnerships with high-volume fabrication facilities so that devices developed in-house transfer cleanly to production at scale. Continue to develop Helion's existing device vendor relationships

ashby:insitro.com:9d864452-e514-47ca-a77.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

insitro is looking for a senior finance leader to build and run our FP&A function, and to take what is already an AI-forward finance capability into the next generation of FP&A. We've done the work of embedding AI across finance; this role owns taking that foundation further so the business has seamless access to information and makes faster, better-informed decisions.

Your year-one priorities: move us from a bi-annual budget to a rolling quarterly forecast; make scenario planning routine enough that the Executive Team sees the budget impact of a decision in days, not weeks; extend our AI-enabled, self-serve FP&A capability; and tighten the partnership with Accounting so planning, close, and reporting run as one system.

You'll own the company-wide budget and forecast, the headcount and compensation model, and the financial materials for the Executive Team and Board, and you'll present directly to the Board. You'll partner closely with Research, Platform, Clinical Development, People, and G&A, serve as a standing partner to Accounting leadership, and work tightly with Investor Relations, Corporate Strategic Finance, and Corporate Development to keep the internal plan and the external financial narrative consistent.

Based in South San Francisco, this position reports to the CFO, leads the FP&A team (today, our Director of R&D and Clinical FP&A), and offers an in-person hybrid schedule of three days per week, on average.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

Planning, Forecasting & Scenario Analysis

 - Own the Planning Cycle: Run the planning calendar end to end, covering the annual operating plan, quarterly reforecasts, and the long-range plan.

 - Rolling Forecast: Lead the shift from a bi-annual budget to a rolling quarterly forecast.

 - Bottom-Up Budget: Build the annual budget across Research, Platform and Compute, Clinical Development, lab operations, and G&A.

 - Scenario Planning: Make scenario planning a standing capability that quantifies the budget impact of decisions before commitments are made.

Next-Generation FP&A & Finance Systems

Slash is building the future of business banking, one industry at a time. We think businesses deserve financial infrastructure built around how they actually operate. MAKING THE METALS POWERING THE WORLD

Solcoa is building the next generation of American metalmaking, starting with rare earths — the metals of power and motion. We've developed a new chemistry that converts rare earth oxides into high-purity metals — the materials inside every EV, fighter jet, wind turbine, and data center — cleaner, cheaper, and faster than any conventional process. Now we're scaling it to thousands of tonnes of annual production.

 


THE ROLE

Head of Engineering will lead Solcoa's Engineering team with the goal of developing and scaling up novel rare earth metal production processes. You will own a full metal production development program. This includes development starting from research, process development, and full scale reactor design. You will also own the engineering, construction, and commissioning of Solcoa’s first commercial facility.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Process Design. Own the design of the metal production process that will bring metal production to cost parity with China. In this capacity, you will identify bottlenecks and radically simplify Solcoa’s process.

 - Reactor Design. You will lead the design and engineering of the modular high-temperature metallothermic reduction reactors capable of producing rare earths at high yield and high throughput. You will organize the research, simulations, and mechanical engineering teams for the engineering and fabrication of it.

 - Solcoa One, Process Design. You will identify key requirements, milestones, and be responsible for the delivery of the operating process at Solcoa One, our first commercial metal production plant. Head of Engineering will lead the process engineering team, responsible for designing the process and balancing of the plant. You will work with the Head of Capital Projects to engineer, staff, commission, and ramp up the largest rare earth metal production plant in the United States.

 - Organization. You will define weekly goals and long-term milestones for the individual contributors on the research team, process development team, and mechanical engineering team. You will identify hiring needs and capital budget needs for achieving the metal capacity goals set by Solcoa’s leadership. You participate in the major decisions that define the direction of Solcoa’s metal production business.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive base salary.

 - Generous stock options.

 - Comprehensive medical, dental and vision insurance.

 - Company-provided lunch daily.

 - Visa sponsorship available if needed.

ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.


About the Role
We are looking for a Head of AI Native Operations to build the autonomous systems that run Supabase.


Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system, where agents carry the operational load end to end. We are standing up a new central team to build that platform and run it in production. This is the role that leads it, and it is hands-on. You design the architecture, build the first versions of the critical pieces, and are accountable for whether every agent we run is correct, safe, and improving over time. We build rather than buy, and there are no settled best practices for most of this yet, so you will be setting them.

You will lead a team of senior individual contributors extending the platform and driving adoption across teams.

What You’ll Be Responsible For
In this role, you’ll:

 - Own the agent platform architecture: The harness and orchestration layer and connectors into company systems, shared context and memory, and the path from prototype to production.

 - Catch regressions before they ship: Model, prompt, and tool changes can’t ship until they pass the evals. When a new model comes out, you know within hours whether to adopt it.

 - Make every agent observable: Every run and every decision is traced. For any agent at any time, you can answer what it did, why, what it cost, and how its quality is trending.

 - Own safety and trust: Design the controls that let agents act without a human in the loop: least-privilege credentials, hard policy limits, escalation thresholds, audit logs, sandboxing, and prompt-injection defenses.

 - Replace workflows, don’t assist them: Pick the workflows agents can fully own today and take them to production.

 - Turn wins into a platform: Package what works into reusable components, templates, and eval harnesses so other teams can ship their own production agents without starting from scratch.

 - Build and direct the team: Hire and grow senior ICs, review their designs and pull requests, and hold the quality bar.

 - Measure what matters: Track workflows automated, eval pass rates, cost per run, and work absorbed against the hiring plan.



How You’ll Think


A Point of View on Where Automation Wins
You have a thesis about how AI and automation change the way a company operates, and it comes from building, not reading. You can look at a business and say which workflows agents can own today, which they will own in 12 months as models improve, and which still need people, and why. You defend that view with evidence from systems you have shipped, and you update it when the evals tell you to.


Eval-Driven
You don’t trust an agent because the demo looked good. You trust it because it passes a test set

Description:

**About Us**

At Allegacy, our digital channels are how most members experience us every day — opening an account on their phone, getting help through chat or voice, managing money in online and mobile banking. These experiences are the front door to Allegacy, and increasingly, they are where we win or lose the member relationship.

We believe digital operations is where member experience, technology, and competitive strategy meet. It’s not only about keeping platforms running — it’s about running them brilliantly: launching new capabilities ahead of the market, resolving issues before members ever feel them, and making every digital interaction easier than the last. That means building a fintech ecosystem that expands what members can do, and putting AI to work to make every experience simpler, faster, and more personal.

**The Opportunity**

We’re seeking a Vice President of Digital Operations to lead the strategy, operation, and growth of Allegacy’s digital banking ecosystem. Reporting to the CIO and serving as a key member of the technology leadership team, you’ll own the platforms, partnerships, and performance of the channels that power digital banking, online account opening, and conversational (chat and voice) experiences — including strategic partners such as Lumin, Glide, and Glia.

This is an enterprise digital leadership role. You’ll set the vision for how Allegacy shows up digitally, architect a fintech ecosystem that creates real market advantage, and put AI to work at scale — from intelligent self-service to agent-assisted and agentic member experiences. You’ll build and lead a growing digital operations organization, own the digital budget and partner portfolio, and bring deep fintech fluency: knowing which partners to bet on, how to structure those relationships, and when to build, buy, partner, or walk away.

This role requires a leader who can move seamlessly between executive strategy, fintech market insight, and operational rigor — influencing peers across Retail, Marketing, Lending, Data & Analytics, and Risk, and translating digital strategy into measurable business outcomes. Success here is measured in digital adoption, member growth, satisfaction, reliability, and efficiency — not lines of code.

**What You’ll Own**

**Digital Strategy & Channel Leadership**

* Define and execute Allegacy’s multi-year digital channel strategy, aligning digital banking, account opening, and conversational channels with enterprise growth goals and the technology roadmap.

Overview:

**ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.**

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

Responsibilities:

**THE ROLE:**

AMD’s Cores Organization delivers industry-leading CPUs, Caches, and Chiplets that are the foundation of AMD’s server, client, and gaming business. We are looking for an experienced Director of Silicon Design Engineering to provide technical and organizational leadership for advanced CPU/core silicon engineering, with responsibility spanning silicon development, validation, post-silicon execution, debug, infrastructure, and cross-functional engineering coordination. Work closely with RTL, Design Verification, Physical Design, DFT, validation, diagnostics, and other engineering organizations to coordinate technical execution and drive cross-functional decisions. The candidate will join the leadership team based in Fort Collins, CO.

**THE PERSON:**

The candidate is a proven leader of leaders with a track record of delivering complex, high-performance cache or CPU designs to production silicon on aggressive schedules. They connect pre-silicon design and verification activities with post-silicon execution, ensuring that technical issues, engineering risks, schedules, methodologies, and silicon readiness are understood and driven to closure across multiple engineering disciplines. We are pushing the envelope on every program, so the status quo must be challenged continuously. This environment requires creativity, innovation, sound judgment, and excellent verbal and written communication skills with engineers, architects, partner organizations, and senior executives alike. The candidate is passionate about building high-performing teams: hiring top talent, developing managers and senior technical leaders, and creating a culture of ownership, collaboration, and accountability. Our team delivers critical designs for multiple AMD products and is growing in both capability and size, so the candidate must be able to scale the organization while keeping execution sharp.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Provide technical leadership across complex silicon design, validation, debug, and bring-up activities.
* Drive resolution of cross-functional technical issues spanning RTL, DV, physical design, DFT, diagnostics, and silicon validation.
* Maintain visibility into silicon readiness, engineering risks, execution dependencies, and issues requiring management attention.
* Participate in major program and methodology decisions affecting current and future CPU/core development
*

As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**About the role**
------------------

The Director, Production Analytics owns Production Analytics globally: every site, every product line, and every production function across Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain, Planning, and Warehousing / Material Management. The ambition is not better dashboards. It is that a division leader can tell whether they will hit rate before they miss it, and that when we argue about where to invest, the argument is settled by data rather than by whoever presents best.

### **ABOUT THE JOB**

This is a player-coach role. You will lead the hardest analytical problems yourself, on the programs that matter most to the company, and build a team that can run several more in parallel. You will be judged on what you accomplish, not on how you operate: whether a program hit rate that would otherwise have slipped, whether a constraint got cleared because we saw it coming, whether a number leadership used to make a real decision came from this team.  
We weigh approach over domain familiarity. The strongest analytics leaders we have are exceptional at how they attack a problem, even where they arrived without the functional background. Manufacturing depth is useful and listed below as preferred, but it does not substitute for analytical method, judgment about what matters, and the ability to drive a result through an organization.

**What you'll do**

---------------------------------

**The Executive Office of Technology Services and Security (EOTSS)** is the lead enterprise technology organization for the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Charged with driving the ongoing alignment of business and technology across the Commonwealth’s Executive Branch, EOTSS oversees and manages the enterprise technology, digital infrastructure and services, as well as the Commonwealth Security Operations Center and an enterprise Standard Operating Environment that includes an information security and risk management framework for over 125 state agencies and over 43,000 state employees. The Director is accountable for building and developing an effective engineering organization, establishing clear priorities and expectations, and ensuring the reliability, security, and long-term sustainability of the platform.

A major focus of this role is strengthening the Commonwealth's internal engineering and operational capabilities. **The Napa Valley**
-------------------

Napa County is home to 140,000 residents who share a strong sense of community and a legacy of preserving and protecting our rich agricultural heritage. Located in the heart of California's preeminent wine region, the Napa Valley is also part of the dynamic San Francisco Bay Metropolitan Area. With its sunny Mediterranean climate and proximity to the mountains and ocean, the Napa Valley offers residents easy access to virtually unlimited shopping, dining, cultural and recreational opportunities. The Napa Valley's strategic location, natural and cultural resources, history of responsible land use planning and attractive quality of life provide the ideal mix of small town living and big city amenities.

**Napa County as an Employer**
------------------------------

As an organization, Napa County is dedicated to improving the lives of our citizens and reflecting the best of the community's values: Respect, Accountability, Dedication, Integrity and Innovation. **LEARN MORE HERE** **and** **Discover the Difference you can make!**

**The Position**

Cresset is a firm built by clients, for clients. As an independent, award-winning multi-family office and private investment firm, we are reimagining the way wealth is experienced. Our purpose is to help ensure that both wealth and life are fully optimized\*\*—integrated, intentional, and aligned with each client’s vision of success.

* Ensure AI solutions are production-ready, reliable, and aligned with enterprise architecture standards.

**Technology Integration & Architecture**

* Partner with Technology and Data teams to integrate AI capabilities into enterprise systems.

* Ensure seamless interoperability across internally built systems and third-party platforms.

Deep Fission is a nuclear technology company pioneering the development of a revolutionary deep borehole pressurized water reactor. We recently completed a private placement financing and Alternative Public Offering and are now operating as a public company while maintaining our startup agility and innovation focus. With strategic partnerships in place, strong private and public investment, and active engagement with the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), we are executing our next phase of growth as we advance our groundbreaking nuclear technology toward commercial deployment.

**JOB SUMMARY/PURPOSE**

Deep Fission is seeking a VP of Engineering to build and lead the technical organization responsible for taking our borehole reactor design from concept to repeatable commercial deployment. This role owns engineering execution across the nuclear steam supply system (NSSS) and surface power conversion, including reactor and mechanical design, nuclear analysis, instrumentation and controls (I&C), and surface support systems. The position will partner closely with our regulatory team on design basis and licensing content for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and the Department of Energy (DOE). The VP will also work closely with our drilling and completions team, which owns the borehole, and the two will jointly own the reactor to borehole interface. Deloitte Global is the engine of the Deloitte network. Our professionals reach across disciplines and borders to develop and lead global initiatives. We deliver strategic programs and services that unite our organization.  
  
**Work you'll do**  
  
Deloitte Global is seeking an experienced technology leader to lead the strategy, architecture, delivery, and continued evolution of our enterprise Salesforce platform and solutions.  
  
As the **Director, Salesforce Delivery & Architecture**, you will set the technical and delivery direction for Salesforce, translate business priorities into a scalable platform roadmap, and lead global teams across architecture, engineering, delivery, and operations. You will partner closely with senior business, product, and technology leaders and serve as a trusted advisor on platform strategy, investment, innovation, and execution.  
  
This role combines **Salesforce platform leadership, enterprise architecture, global delivery, governance, and technology strategy** and is ideal for a leader who can connect technical decisions to measurable business outcomes.

* Define and lead the **Salesforce platform strategy, architecture, and multi-year technology roadmap**, aligning investments and capabilities with business and technology priorities.
* Provide technical and delivery leadership across Salesforce solutions, integrations, and related enterprise platforms.
* Lead global delivery teams through solution architecture, engineering, implementation, release, operations, and continuous improvement.
* Establish architecture principles, engineering standards, and technical decision-making practices that enable scalable, secure, resilient, and maintainable solutions.
* Partner with business sponsors, product owners, architects, and engineering teams to translate business priorities into platform capabilities and delivery plans.
* Lead demand management, prioritization, and roadmap decisions across the Salesforce portfolio.
* Provide leadership for major Salesforce implementations, enhancements, modernization efforts, and platform lifecycle initiatives.
* Guide integration strategy across Salesforce and enterprise applications, including APIs, middleware, data platforms, and cloud services.
* Champion Agile delivery, DevOps, and CI/CD practices to improve delivery speed, platform quality, reliability, and performance.
* Evaluate emerging Salesforce capabilities, including **Agentforce and AI-enabled solutions**, and identify opportunities to apply them responsibly to business needs.
* Define and track KPIs that measure platform performance, delivery outcomes, investment value, and value realization.
* Lead technology budgeting, forecasting, resource planning, vendor management, and strategic technology partnerships.
* Identify and manage technical, operational, financial, and delivery risks and ensure appropriate governance and mitigation plans are maintained.
* Build trusted-advisor relations

We are EnduroSat! A fast-growing space scale-up at the forefront of satellite innovation, specializing in advanced software-flexible satellites for commercial, governmental, and scientific endeavors.

* **This is more than a job, it's a mission**

  We are making space universally accessible and redefining the possible
* **We get things done**

  We take ownership of what we do and we work hard to make a difference
* **We are fearless**

**What is the role?**

As our VP of Engineering & Chief Engineer, you will own the final technical delivery of EnduroSat US across hundreds of missions and the engineering organization that creates it. Systems engineering, mechanical, structural and FEA, thermal, software, and the other disciplines all report to you. You hold final technical authority on US programs: you decide what the system looks like, you sign off on the final architecture, and you are accountable when it does not work.  
  
The engineering problem here is not clean-sheet design. Our satellites share a common platform, and the value we deliver is the last mile on top of it — the integration, and mission-specific design that turns a proven bus into a spacecraft that does a particular customer's job. You will assess whether our existing system design can meet a given mission, decide where it must change, and conceive adapted or new capability where it cannot. That takes deeper judgment than drawing from scratch, because every decision must survive contact with a platform, a schedule, and a supply chain that already exist.  
  
You will be in front of customers regularly — large commercial, civil, and defense organizations whose engineering teams will test whether our answers hold up. You will shape mission concepts during capture, defend architectures at PDR and CDR, and make requirements less dumb. You need the depth to take final decisions yourself and exceptional focus to ignore the noise so a mission can achieve what it needs on time and on budget, not the perfect solution that never comes.  
  
You will work as a peer to our VP of Mission & Programs, who owns delivery and the program relationship. You own what we build and whether it will work; they own getting it delivered and flown. You will also be in close contact with the European technological leadership who own the platform you are building on — keeping US and European engineering aligned on standards, architecture, and interfaces is part of this job, not an afterthought.

**Job Description Summary**
===========================

As part of the GE Aerospace Digital Technology organization supporting the Defense & Systems (D&S) business, the Director of DevOps, Support, and Operations keeps the Defense and Systems Customer Experience (DSCX) application portfolio secure, reliable, and compliant. This is a people-leadership role accountable for vulnerability remediation, reliability (SLA, SLO, and SLI), automation and toil reduction, vendor management, defect management, legacy lifecycle and sunsetting, and resilience and continuity including on-call and disaster recovery. This person will lead a team of operations and application engineers and set the operational discipline for the portfolio.

**Job Description**
===================

**Why This Role Exists**

DSCX owns 30+ digital products for Defense & Systems. Today our technical product managers wear three hats for their products: product management, project management, and operations. We are dividing that load across three dedicated functions, and this role will build out the operations discipline, consolidating ticket management, software hygiene, patching, and vulnerability closure into a single team. This role is planned to have 6-8 direct reports, and the portfolio includes many legacy applications and reports that need to be retired, rewritten, or absorbed into our AI product vision. Vulnerability and high priority defect findings come from the Defense & Systems security organization under the BISO, and closing them inside the severity SLA, including CMMC obligations on affected products, is part of this team's accountability. Your charge is to standardize processes and artifacts, build automation that removes the manual work, and then coach and train your team to hold it. You should be experienced with AI and know where it creates opportunity to expand what the team can deliver.

**Environment**

The DSCX portfolio runs primarily on AWS, Palantir Foundry, or through SaaS based 3rd party solutions, with on-premise implementations supported for customers whose data sensitivity requires it. Delivery runs through Rally and Microsoft Teams and ServiceNow is our system of record for incident, change, and defect management. Monitoring and alerting tooling varies by application across the portfolio, and consolidating it is part of this team's work. Finally, the portfolio carries a $25+MM annual budget across our product line.

**Roles and Responsibilities**  
  
**Security and Vulnerability Remediation**

* Own vulnerability remediation and high-priority application defects across the DSCX portfolio, working against the policy, scanning cadence, and severity SLAs set by the Defense & Systems Business Information Security Officer (BISO), who is the source for both.
* Accountable for getting DSCX applications compliant against the BISO's D&S-wide program, including CMMC obligations on affected products.
* Own the remediation backlog with a named owner and target date

Karman is a fast-growing NVIDIA-backed AI company enabling AI data centers to dynamically orchestrate power and unlock more compute capacity from existing energy infrastructure. For over a decade, we have applied AI to the electric grid, bringing real-time visibility and power-flow control to complex energy infrastructure. Our Karman platform, built on a custom NVIDIA module, brings that same capability to AI data centers, giving operators a way to better use the power already available to them.  
  
**The team**  
The Power Applications team takes power orchestration algorithms from idea to production. We develop, ship, and maintain the applications that run on Karman to solve power management problems and orchestrate control actions in real time in megawatt-scale data centers. We own the decision layer of Karman’s real-time control loop: turning live power telemetry into power management commands fast enough to keep data centers safe and fully utilized.  
  
Our scope requires us to blend research and development with continuous delivery. The team is a mix of data scientists, algorithms engineers, software engineers, and AI infrastructure engineers, organized into two complementary groups. Research and development proves and matures new control, estimation, and forecasting capabilities and builds the evidence to decide what moves into the product. Continuous delivery turns that validated theory into reliable, deployable software and keeps it performing in the field.  
  
**The role**  
The Director, Power Applications leads this team and owns its outcomes on both workflows, reporting to the VP of AI and Applications.  
  
The job sits at the interface between research and implementation. On one side you lead scientists and senior algorithms engineers working on open problems, where the hardest questions are how to interpret, prioritize, and resource work with ambiguous scope, and when to pivot, double down, or shelve. On the other side you lead principal-level software engineers shipping control software with hard reliability guarantees against committed product dates. Your job is to make those two sides one program: research framed so that it produces decisions on time, results that move into production as deliberate increments, and field performance that feeds the next research question.  
  
You are also the team's single point of contact for planning and reporting. **Description**

The Homeland Sector operates across some of the world's most consequential transportation, security, infrastructure and government missions.

Its portfolio spans air traffic management, airports and borders, security screening, energy and critical infrastructure, and substantial businesses in the United States, United Kingdom and Australia. Across these markets, customers are modernizing long-lived operational systems while adopting software, data, AI and other rapidly evolving technologies.

Technology must therefore do more than support individual programs. It must help shape where Homeland competes, how it grows, what it invests in and how it improves execution.

The Homeland Sector CTO is responsible for making that happen.

This is an enterprise business and technology leadership role. The CTO helps shape business and portfolio strategy, engages customers before requirements are fixed, creates technology-enabled growth opportunities, strengthens major pursuits and execution, and builds the technical leadership and capabilities required for Homeland's future.

As a member of the Corporate CTO organization and the senior technology executive for Homeland, this leader connects enterprise technology strategy and capabilities with the customer, market and delivery needs of the Sector.

The opportunity is to help lead and change the Homeland business using technology as a principal lever for growth, differentiation, speed and performance.

Position Summary

The Chief Technology Officer of the Homeland Sector is responsible for shaping how technology advances the Sector's strategy, growth, delivery, investment priorities and future portfolio.

  

The CTO reports to the Leidos Corporate CTO, with a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Homeland Sector President. The Corporate CTO owns enterprise technology strategy, architecture, standards and enterprise capabilities. The Homeland Sector President owns Sector business strategy and outcomes. The Homeland CTO is accountable for integrating those agendas and for technology outcomes across the Homeland business.

The CTO serves as both a senior leader within Corporate Technology and a member of the Homeland Sector executive leadership team. The role directly leads the Homeland technology organization, including the Business Area CTOs and cross-sector technical leaders, and works closely with Business Area presidents, Growth, Operations and corporate technology organizations.

The role creates value in both directions: bringing relevant Leidos technologies, platforms, talent and investment into Homeland while ensuring Homeland's customer needs, technologies and market insights help shape the broader Leidos technology agenda.

The mandate is not to impose common technology for its own sake. It is to create leverage where shared platforms, capabilities, talent and investment provide real advantage while preserving the domain expertise and flexibility required by distinct businesses.

**Job Summary**:

The Director of Quality Assurance leads the QA organization through its transformation to an AI-optimized SDLC, able to support multiple product launches and continuous feature delivery in parallel across a multi-tenant SaaS platform. This leader defines the overarching quality strategy, champions the integration of AI tools across the entire SDLC, and scales automated, resilient testing frameworks to accelerate delivery while sustaining the reliability and regulatory compliance Medrio's customers depend on. This position reports directly to the SVP of Engineering and works closely with Development, Product, Support, and Compliance throughout the SDLC. The QA organization is geographically dispersed, combining onshore and offshore teams of in-house engineers and external vendor partners working across multiple time zones.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* **AI-Driven Quality Strategy:** Lead the strategic integration of generative and predictive AI tools throughout the SDLC, including AI-assisted test case creation, requirements analysis, and automated risk-based test coverage.
* **Quality Throughput & Capacity:** Scale quality output in line with an AI-accelerated development organization, ensuring test capacity keeps pace with development output without compromising quality. Success is measured through cycle time to release, escaped defect rate, automated test coverage, and full regression suite runtime.
* **Modern Test Automation Leadership:** Oversee the evolution of automated testing strategies for a multi-tenant SaaS platform, prioritizing modern frameworks like Playwright alongside AI-powered self-healing test infrastructure to minimize script maintenance and maximize suite reliability. This includes tenant isolation and data-segregation testing, configuration-driven test matrices across tenant variants, and management of shared-schema regression risk.
* **Organization Oversight:** Direct all activities of the QA organization, ensuring continuous validation, high platform stability, and alignment with modern quality engineering best practices.
* **Regulatory & Compliance Quality:** Ensure QA practices, documentation, and evidence meet the requirements of a regulated healthcare environment (including HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11, GxP/CSV, SOC 2, and GDPR where applicable), and support internal and customer audits as a senior representative of the quality function.
* **Validation of AI-Generated Test Assets:** Own the framework by which AI-assisted test artifacts are reviewed, approved, and evidenced, ensuring automation generated with AI meets the traceability and audit standards required in a validated environment.
* **Security-Forward Quality:** Partner with Security and DevOps to embed security testing into the delivery pipeline (SAST/DAST, dependency and vulnerability triage, and coordination of penetration testing), and ensure PHI is appropriately handled and de-identified across test environments and test data.

Our team is boldly redefining power generation to accelerate the world's energy transition. We operate as one team, pushing toward our vision of the future. With a substantial installed base and multi-decade service agreements, our business depends on a resilient, modern ERP backbone that connects manufacturing, project installation, field service, supply chain, and finance at enterprise scale.

  

Having completed the foundational upgrade from SAP ECC 6.0, we are now entering a high-impact phase: deploying new S/4HANA functionality and modules, modernizing our data and integration architecture, and embedding AI-driven capabilities into day-to-day operations. The Director of IT ERP is the senior technology leader accountable for the strategy, architecture, deployment, and ongoing operation of the S/4HANA platform and its surrounding enterprise application ecosystem (SAP BTP, SAP Ariba, data and integration services). Pedestal Health (formerly Target RWE) is a rapidly growing company at the intersection of clinical research, healthcare, and technology, focused on reimagining clinical evidence generation. Description:

Scale Computing is the leader in edge computing, virtualization, and hyperconverged solutions for customers around the globe. The company transforms the way businesses use infrastructure technology through the delivery of innovative products and services, with a philosophy of innovation and employee empowerment driving its commitment to best-in-class customer experiences, partner success, and shareholder return. Employees, known internally as "Scalers," operate by five core values: Vigilant, Owner, Integrity, Champion, and Empower.

**About the Role**

Scale Computing is hiring a Director of IT to lead corporate IT: the end-user services, identity, endpoints, collaboration and business SaaS (software-as-a-service) platforms, office networks, and IT service desk that every Scaler depends on. This leader owns how IT work is taken in, prioritized, delivered, and reported, and is accountable for the cost, reliability, and security of the corporate technology estate.

This is a full-time in-office role based in our Austin, TX or Indianapolis, IN offices.

The strongest candidates have consolidated IT environments after an acquisition, can explain in detail how they run planned and unplanned IT work, and measure success by outcomes delivered and cost removed rather than tickets closed.

**What You'll Do**

* Own the IT service desk: intake, request catalog, queue structure, prioritization, SLA (service level agreement) definition and attainment, and knowledge base.
* Consolidate duplicate workflows inherited from legacy organizations into a single IT service model, and retire the redundant tooling.
* Own identity and access lifecycle for the workforce (Google Workspace, SSO, MFA), including joiner/mover/leaver processes integrated with HR, and least-privilege access in partnership with Security.
* Own endpoint management (MDM, patching, imaging, encryption, EDR deployment coverage) across Windows, macOS, and mobile devices.
* Manage the SaaS portfolio and IT vendors: license utilization, renewals, contract negotiation, rationalization of overlapping tools, and SaaS administration ownership.
* Own IT asset management: hardware lifecycle, procurement standards, inventory accuracy, and secure disposal.
* Own office and remote-worker connectivity, conferencing, and collaboration services across company locations.
* Build and manage the IT budget, with reporting on spend by category, cost per employee, and savings delivered.
* Use AI assistance to reduce IT workload (ticket deflection, triage, knowledge authoring, scripting), and set the team standard for what it is used for and what output is verified.
* Develop the IT team, maintaining a documented development plan and a named ownership area for every team member; address underperformance promptly with documented plans.
* Represent IT in change management, incident escalation, and cross-functional planning with Business Systems, Finance, HR, Platform Infrastructure, and Security.

At Submittable, we are transforming how organizations create social impact. Our platform empowers thousands of mission-driven organizations, from nonprofits to government entities, to make a difference in their communities and beyond. In 2024, our innovative software helped organizations worldwide run **30,000 programs**, welcomed **1.2 million applicants**, and facilitated the distribution of **more than $10 billion** in funding through our products on behalf of our clients.

We are on a mission to help organizations accelerate their impact, so we are proud to partner with organizations focused on Equity & Social Justice, Children & Education, Creative & Arts, Health & Wellness, Economic Justice & Opportunity, and Environment & Climate. ------------------

Submittable is hiring a Vice President of Engineering who is deeply technical, works hands-on, and builds with AI every day. You will report to the CTO and run engineering day to day: delivery, quality, reliability, cost, and the people who make them happen.

We want a different VP than the old SaaS playbook produced. That playbook grew output by growing headcount and adding layers of management. Based at our headquarters in Dupo, Illinois, this role sets the technology, identity, security, and data standard for a growing organization — and carries that standard into every new site and business we acquire. * Drive to Win – We set high standards and take pride in delivering exceptional results.

* Step Up & Take Ownership – Every team member is empowered to take initiative and make an impact.
* Strive to Innovate – Continuous learning and problem-solving keep us at the forefront of our industry.
* We Are Family – Respect, trust, and teamwork define our workplace culture.

At The Goley Companies, you're more than an employee—you're part of a team committed to building excellence together.

The Director of IT is an integral member of the firm’s administrative leadership team and reports to the Executive Director. This role is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the firm’s information technology systems and assisting in the development and implementation of IT initiatives. This role is responsible for the management, training, and development of the personnel within the IT department. * Strong work ethic and personal initiative with a willingness to take ownership of tasks and projects and see them through to their completion.
* Strong strategic thinking skills with the ability to develop and implement policies and procedures.
* Commitment to providing excellent customer service and representing the firm in a professional and courteous manner.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Previous experience in a professional services setting, such as a law or accounting firm.

* Relevant IT or cybersecurity certifications.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead and direct the IT department, ensuring proper staffing, training, development, and resource allocation.
* Oversee hardware and software procurement, deployment, maintenance, replacement, and lifecycle management.
* Establish and enforce appropriate security

Description AI has the potential to transform how insurers bring new products to market. Help us make sure it does. US Data Science (USDS) is building a new team that will use advanced AI to bring our pricing programs to market faster, and we are hiring three senior data scientists to help launch it. The team will build state-of-the-art evaluations for AI and agentic systems. Those evaluations tell us how much value the AI delivers, how accurate it is, and what the risk is when it gets something wrong, so we can move high-value applications into production with confidence. This is a new, highly visible team, and its work will shape how AI is used in the core pricing work of US Retail Markets (USRM). Each of the three roles reports into the Rollout AI team in USDS and has a dotted-line relationship with one of our lines of business: Property & Specialty, Auto, or Small Commercial. You will be the data science partner for your line of business while working as one team with the other two, sharing methods and tools. These roles will be filled at the Assistant Director or Director I level, depending on experience and skills.

**Level of position offered will be based on skills and experience at manager discretion**

This role may have in-office requirements depending on candidate location

**Candidates who live within 50 miles of Boston, MA; Portsmouth, NH; Seattle, WA; Columbus, OH; or Plano, TX will follow a hybrid schedule, coming into the office two days per week. Otherwise, this role is remote with occasional travel.**

Responsibilities:
- Partner with your line of business's pricing, delivery, and technology teams to find where AI can speed up pricing program rollout.
- Build state-of-the-art evaluations for AI and agentic applications. Define accuracy metrics and ground truth, generate statistical tests and edge cases, and design experiments, including tests in production.
- Measure the value and risk of AI applications, including effort reduced, errors avoided, and time to market gained.
- Bring pricing expertise and product sense to AI projects, translating business needs into requirements and evaluation criteria.
- Prototype and build evaluation tooling and, over time, AI applications that accelerate rollout.

The ideal candidate will have:
- Hands-on experience building and deploying insurance pricing models.
- Strong expertise in model evaluation, statistics, and experimental design.
- Strong coding skills (for example, Python) and a track record of building and shipping data science solutions.
- Strong, recent hands-on experience with modern LLMs, including but not limited to agentic coding, building LLMs into applications, and/or RAG.
- Experience evaluating generative AI or agentic systems is a plus.
- Strong communication and stakeholder skills, comfortable working across business, delivery, and technology teams.
- Resilient, curious, acts in service of the best answer, holds themselves to a high standard and wants to be around others
