About the Role

Abnormal AI protects organizations from the most sophisticated email and collaboration attacks using behavioral AI. Security is not a bolt-on at Abnormal; it is core to the product we sell and the trust our customers place in us. Our security organization operates a commercial cloud environment and a separate FedRAMP-authorized environment, and we are pursuing increasingly rigorous federal authorizations as we grow.

We are hiring a Director of Security reporting to the CISO and leading the Security Engineering organization. You will build and scale high-performing security teams, own major security programs end to end, and operate autonomously in the CISO's absence, including representing security to executive leadership, customers, and auditors.

This is a role for a deeply technical leader with a software engineering background who has grown into people leadership. You have built security teams from the ground up, you write and review code and architecture when it matters, and you believe the best security organizations earn their influence through partnership rather than policy enforcement.

Our Security Philosophy

We run security the way the best engineering-led companies do:
- Security reduces toil. Our job is to make the rest of the company faster and safer at the same time. If a control adds friction without reducing risk, it is a defect.
- Paved paths, safe by default. We invest in guardrails, golden paths, and secure-by-default infrastructure so the easy choice is the secure choice. We prefer preventing classes of problems over chasing individual findings.
- Partnership over gatekeeping. Security succeeds only through deep collaboration with engineering, IT, and business teams. We embed with builders, we ship alongside them, and we take on their constraints as our own.
- Engineering-grade rigor. We treat security problems as engineering problems: automated, measurable, code-reviewed, and continuously improved.

If the security cultures that value freedom and responsibility, context over control, and guardrails over gates resonate with you, you will feel at home here.

What You Will Do
- Serve as deputy to the CISO: act with full authority in the CISO's absence and represent the security organization to executives, customers, and regulators.
- Lead, coach, and grow managers and senior engineers across Security Engineering and Security Operations.
- Own the security engineering roadmap: cloud security architecture (AWS-first), detection and response, identity, vulnerability management, and secure-by-default platform investments.
- Drive cross-functional programs with Engineering, IT, and Product, from AI security governance to data perimeter controls to federal compliance initiatives.
- Set and defend engineering standards for the security organization: everything as code, automated where possible, measured against outcomes rather than activity.
- Build hiring pipelines and raise the bar on every hire; own performance man

Alta Resource Technologies (Alta) is a next generation mining company that uses synthetic biology to separate critical minerals from conventional and unconventional resources, including e-waste. Founded in 2023, the company is expanding its team in Boulder, CO. The exponential growth of new tech industries, as well as the information technology sector, are driving historic growth in mineral demand and stressing existing supply streams. Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Who We Are

Atwell, LLC is a bold leader in the consulting, engineering, and construction services industry, delivering a broad range of creative solutions to clients in the real estate & land development, and energy markets. We have a strong national presence and a diverse, award-winning project portfolio. Atwell is a privately owned company, with 2,000+ passionate team members across 75+ locations and growing!

Atwell, LLC  is a proud recipient of the following 2025  awards:
- Ten consecutive years in a row as a “Best Place to Work” by Zweig Group (#11)
- Recognized as #70 in the ENR Top 500 Design Firms, ranked in every region
- Recognized in Crain's “Fast 50” as one of the fastest-growing companies (#14)
- Recognized as the 2025 ENR Design Firm of the year for the Southeastern US

Job Description

As the Director of Civil Engineering for Land Development, you will lead business development initiatives, manage a talented team of engineers and support staff, and spearhead the regional strategy for our land development projects. This role requires a visionary leader with a strong background in civil engineering, a proven track record in land development, and exceptional leadership and business development skills.

Key Responsibilities:
- Leadership & Management:
- Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of civil engineers and support staff.
- Foster a collaborative and innovative work environment that encourages professional growth and development.
- Oversee the planning, design, and execution of land development projects, ensuring adherence to quality, budget, and timeline requirements.
- Develop and execute regional strategies to drive growth and profitability in the land development market.
- Business Development:
- Develop and implement strategic business development plans to expand our market presence and secure new land development projects.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with key clients, stakeholders, and industry partners.
- Identify and pursue new business opportunities, including preparing proposals, presentations, and negotiations.
- Represent the company at industry events, conferences, and meetings to enhance our visibility and reputation.
- Project Management:
- Ensure the successful delivery of land development projects from inception to completion.
- Coordinate with internal and external teams to ensure seamless project execution and client satisfaction.

Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field
- Professional Engineer (PE) license required.
- Minimum of 15 years of experience in civil engineering, focusing on land development (commercial and/or SFD).
- Proven track record in business development and client relationship management.
- Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate a diverse team.
- Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills.
- Strategic thinker with the ability to develop and execute long-term plans.

AXS connects fans with the artists and teams they love. Each year we sell millions of tickets to thousands of incredible events – from concerts and festivals to sports and theater – at some of the most iconic venues in the world. Since our founding in 2011, we’ve consistently pushed the industry forward and improved experiences for fans, making it easier than ever to discover events, find the perfect seats, and enjoy unforgettable live entertainment, and we continue to lead the evolution of our industry today.

We’re passionate about improving the fan experience and providing game-changing solutions for our clients, and we’re always looking for smart, motivated people to help make it happen. Bring your enthusiasm, your big ideas, and your desire to team up with some of the best and brightest in technology and entertainment.

About The Role
We're looking for a Sr. Director of Engineering to lead and grow the team behind AX’s next generation of B2B tools. You will lead the team on a multi- year journey building best in class application that enables our live event customers to create, configure, sell, and manage events

You'll partner closely with your product counterpart to shape both the direction of the product and the underlying technology that makes it possible; sequencing the work, derisking the hard problems, and making the architectural calls that serve fans and clients at scale. This is a high-growth, fast-paced charter: the demands on the platform are growing quickly, and your job is to build the team and the systems to stay ahead of that demand.

Just as importantly, you'll grow the people under you — developing engineers and emerging leaders so the team's bench deepens as the charter expands. This is a hands on position where you will drive results through small teams of highly capable people and through leveraging AI to scale yourself and your teams.

Responsibilities

Bevi is on a mission to transform how beverages are delivered and consumed. Our connected beverage platform eliminates the need for single-use bottles and cans, making it easy, fun, and sustainable to stay hydrated. As the category leader in IoT-enabled beverage technology, we're building a future where Bevi machines are everywhere people live, work, and connect. We've raised over $160M in venture capital, serve thousands of customers across the US, Canada, UK and Ireland, and we've been rapidly growing year over year, saving over 1 billion bottles from waste. In addition to driving hypergrowth with our current product line, Bevi is heavily investing in new product development.

We are hiring a Director of Program Management to lead Bevi's central PMO. The PMO runs our new product introduction (NPI) programs from concept to launch. The team includes five program managers and sits in Operations, reporting to the COO.

This is a leadership role and a hands-on one. You will lead and develop the team, set the standard for how Bevi runs hardware programs, and run one of our most important NPI programs yourself. Our goal is to reduce our NPI cycle time with a higher predictability and quality. This role is central to getting there.

Your Day to Day

Lead the PMO
- Lead, coach and grow a team of program managers running complex, cross-functional hardware programs.
- Set the standard for how Bevi runs NPI programs and hold the team to it.
- Own Bevi's phase gate process. Each gate ends in a clear go, no-go or recycle decision, and open items carry forward with owners.

Run programs well
- Lead by example, taking on NPI programs directly as needed while building the team.
- Make sure every program has an aggressive, credible schedule that the team believes in and that is updated every week.
- Name risks early, assign owners and track the inputs that drive them: drawings, test results, open decisions and supplier dates.
- Base status on evidence (test data, released drawings, placed POs), not verbal updates. Raise issues before dates are missed, with options.
- Get the right people in the room to make decisions, and log them.
- Report program status to the leadership team and the Board.

Work across the company
- Partner with Product, Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Service and Sales so programs launch at target quality, cost and supply readiness.
- Work with the leadership team and Product on portfolio priorities. Make resource and schedule tradeoffs visible so they can decide.
- Manage programs that involve contract manufacturers and design partners, including partners in Asia.

Make the PMO more efficient
- Keep core teams small and meetings focused on decisions and issues.
- Move program information to one system of record, so status is updated once and every report pulls from it.
- Use automation and AI to cut the time PMs spend compiling updates.
- Run post-program reviews and use what we learn to improve the playbook.

Biosphere has a technically ambitious roadmap with concrete milestones: new reactor technologies to de-risk and integrate into our demonstration plant. Your first job is to help us execute on these scoped challenges. You’ll own day-to-day R&D priorities, experimental decisions and delivery within agreed budgets. Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. - Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure SDLC)

The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well. If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team.

Director, Cloud Infrastructure

We're hiring a Director of Cloud Infrastructure to join Convene Hospitality Group's (CHG) Technology organization. It's a hands-on role with an AI-native mindset. There are no direct reports today. You’ll lead through the platform, redesigning how we deploy and setting the standards our product and corporate engineering teams build on. You'll also run the cloud, AI, and venue infrastructure under our portfolio of brands, from client-facing experiences to the systems that keep our nearly 40 venues running. This is a rebuild. You design it and you build it.

Today, deployments are manual and happen about once a sprint. That's the starting line. You'll rethink how we ship so that deployments are unlocked, safe, secure, and governed.

You'll have high autonomy and real decision-making power over the tools we use and how we build. We're committed to AWS and will build deeply on it. GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description

The systems our OT clients run treat drinking water, move natural gas, run production lines, and keep hospital equipment working. Many were installed before anyone thought about attackers, and plenty still run software the vendor stopped supporting years ago. You can't take a refinery controller offline on a Tuesday afternoon to patch it, and you can't reboot a substation to check whether a fix worked. This work needs people who understand the physical process as well as the network, and we've built a team of them. When we do it well, nobody outside the plant ever hears about it. GuidePoint Security is hiring a Director, OT/IoT Security Services to lead that team.

You'll report to the SVP of Offensive Security and own the practice: the team, the service catalog, delivery quality, and the P&L. The delivery managers already run day-to-day projects well, so expect to spend most of your time with engineers and clients, and to be the senior escalation point when a technical or client issue gets complicated. The rest goes to supporting regional sales teams, other GuidePoint Security practices, and technology partners.

In this practice, "Wow Them" means an account executive gets a scope and price back quickly, our engineers work safely on a running plant floor, and the client calls us for their next site.

About the OT/IoT Security Services Practice

The OT/IoT Security Services practice protects the industrial systems our clients depend on in energy, water, manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, and other critical infrastructure sectors. We deliver in every GuidePoint Security region and provide the services behind GuidePoint Security's OT technology partnerships.

Most of the team came to security from the plant floor or the military: veterans and former engineers from utilities, oil and gas, manufacturing, and nuclear power. They know what an operator is thinking when a consultant walks into the control room with a laptop, and safety and uptime come first on every job.

A typical client relationship starts with finding out what's actually on the OT network and where it's exposed. From there we design segmentation and controls that don't interrupt operations, and many clients stay with us for ongoing OT vulnerability management. About Invisible

Invisible Technologies makes AI work. Our end-to-end AI platform structures messy data, automates digital workflows, deploys agentic solutions, measures outcomes, and integrates human expertise where it matters most.

Our platform cleans, labels, and structures company data so it is ready for AI. It adapts models to each business and adds human expertise when needed, the same approach we have used to improve models for more than 80% of the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, AWS, and Cohere.

Our successes span industries, from supply chain automation for Swiss Gear to AI-enabled naval simulations with SAIC, and validating NBA draft picks for the Charlotte Hornets.

IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. You will set direction for the team, support individual growth, and make sure the group can respond effectively to both immediate operational issues and longer term reliability challenges.

Jetson is on a mission to accelerate the transition of 100 million homes across North America away from fossil fuels toward sustainable energy use. We believe in a future that is 100% electric and 100% better.

Homes are one of the largest sources of carbon emissions, yet adoption of solutions like heat pumps remains slow due to cost and complexity. Jetson is solving this by building the first fully vertically integrated home electrification company — making clean energy simple, transparent, and affordable.

We rely heavily on technology, automation, and data to scale this impact. At Jetson, we value people who are excellent at their craft, curious about new tools (including AI), and motivated to continuously improve how work gets done.

And because service data is the most honest feedback loop in the business, you own pushing what breaks in the field back into equipment selection, install standards, commissioning requirements, and crew training. This is a build-and-run role: you'll be designing the service function while operating it, across multiple markets at once.

This is a working senior leadership role requiring hands-on technical experience and active engagement. The Senior Director establishes technical direction, assigns clear decision authority within the organization, and ensures that consequential engineering decisions have an adequate technical basis and are made by qualified decision-makers. Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in.

About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 102.4 million monthly active users (MAU), as of June 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com .

Life360 is a Remote-First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US) regardless of any specified location above.

Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

The AI Platforms team builds the shared foundation that lets Life360 use AI quickly and safely. Today, that means powering AI adoption and productivity across the company: model access, agent tooling, and the infrastructure our engineers rely on every day. We work side by side with the teams that are reshaping how Life360 builds with agents. We’ll carry these AI foundations as we look forward towards our future AI product strategy.

About the Job

As the Director of AI Platforms, you will build and lead the team through a defining shift: from supporting how Life360 works with AI to powering how AI shows up for our members. You will be a critical leader in our continued evolution for our agentic product development lifecycle (PDLC), turning early momentum into shared platforms, paved roads, and measurable results. Looking forward, you’ll shape how the platform supports AI inference and AI-powered features within our product.

You will report to the Chief Information Security Officer with close partnership across our entire leadership team.

Our mission is to activate autonomous labor at scale and build toward infinitely elastic industrial capacity. We’re a team of engineers, researchers, and operators who have spent our careers working on the hardest problems in AI, robotics, engineering, and autonomous systems. Who we are

The real world is the next frontier, and at Metropolis, we are creating the artificial intelligence to make it responsive. We are pioneering the Recognition Economy — a future where mundane repetition disappears and being known unlocks access, comfort, and belonging everywhere you go. From transforming parking into a seamless drive-in, drive-out experience for millions of Members to expanding our intelligence layer across retail and hospitality, we are building a world that feels instinctive and magical. The future isn’t coming; it’s here, and we need builders, innovators, and problem solvers to help us create it.

Who you are

Metropolis is seeking a Director, Engineering Operations & Strategy to own technology strategy, operational leadership, and strategic problem-solving across our engineering organization. In this role, you will lead with high autonomy, managing a multi-million dollar engineering budget, cutting through deeply complex problems, exhibiting exceptional leadership without authority, and defining simple, scalable solutions to challenging problems at a hyper growth company. You will partner directly with senior leadership to execute M&A due diligence, streamline shared technical processes, and navigate high-stakes operational challenges. The ideal candidate thrives in uncertainty, takes full ownership of outcomes, and brings a unique blend of hands-on technical grounding and high-intensity strategic experience.

What you'll do
- Own shared processes across the engineering department, including hiring workflows, onboarding, and training, to keep practices consistent as the org scales.
- Cut through deeply complex, multifaceted operational challenges to deliver simple, actionable solutions without waiting for top-down instruction
- Direct and manage a $50M a $100million+ P&L budget, coordinating resources to align with high-level corporate objectives
- Own hardware and service forecasting for critical vendors (AWS, Twilio, and similar), maintaining ongoing visibility into spend trends and flagging risks or opportunities before they become urgent.
- Own emerging strategic decisions for the engineering organization — M&A due diligence, major vendor migrations, and similar high-stakes calls — in close partnership with senior executives.
- Build alignment at the highest levels of leadership, navigating the nuances of multi-stakeholder decisions on multifaceted or high-risk initiatives
- Keep teams unblocked and moving forward rapidly, demonstrating comfort acting with incomplete information as long as directionally correct
- Leverage curiosity and formal methodologies to break down cross-functional silos, challenge status-quo assumptions, and drive cross-team alignment
- Forecast operational trends and deliver strategic recommendations that favor proactive disruption over routine maintenance
- Own all vendor management across the engineering organization, from contract negotiation and renewals to performance accountability

greenhouse:pendo:8822008002.description:
The team + the role

Pendo's Data Platform is the backbone of everything we do. Our systems process more than 50 billion events per day, peaking at over 1 million events per second, and manage dozens of petabytes of data across several production environments. The platform powers real-time data ingestion, batch processing, and analytics at scale — and the instrumentation standards that keep our entire codebase observable. It's built primarily in Go, runs on Google Kubernetes Engine, and relies on Cloud Pub/Sub, Firestore, Google Cloud Storage, Redis, and memcache. We expect the stack to evolve, and you'll help decide how.

We're looking for a Director of Engineering to lead the teams that own this infrastructure. This is a leadership role with real technical depth — you'll set strategy, build and grow high-performing engineering teams, and partner closely with Site Reliability Engineering. You'll stay close enough to the code to review designs, debug production issues, and contribute when it matters. You'll also own the economics of running the platform at this scale and be a trusted voice with customers on performance, data integrity, and reliability. If you want a role where architectural decisions have immediate business consequence and the technical bar is genuinely high, this is it.

This role is based in Raleigh, NC and follows Pendo's hybrid model: in-office 3 days per week.

What this looks like day-to-day
- Lead multiple engineering teams responsible for our real-time data ingestion pipeline, analytics batch job pipelines, and analytics query engine — setting technical direction and roadmap while balancing near-term delivery with long-term scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency.
- Drive architectural decisions across storage, compute, and data modeling; know when to adopt, build, or retire technologies and make those calls with conviction and clear rationale.
- Own instrumentation standards across the core codebase — structured logging, OpenTelemetry metrics and tracing — ensuring teams across the organization can adopt them with minimal friction and that the resulting telemetry is useful, consistent, and cost-conscious.
- Own the cost profile of the data platform at petabyte scale: forecast infrastructure spend for new product initiatives, improve cost attribution by customer, product, feature, and team, and diagnose and resolve cost overruns quickly.
- Partner with SRE on shared on-call responsibilities, incident response, postmortems, and reliability roadmaps; define and track SLOs for ingestion latency, query performance, and data correctness.
- Serve as a technical authority in customer conversations on platform performance, data integrity, and reliability — translating customer needs and escalations into clear engineering priorities.
- Hire, coach, and develop engineering managers and senior engineers; build a team culture grounded in high standards, clear communication, and continuous improvement.

Welcome to Planet. We believe in using space to help life on Earth.

Planet designs, builds, and operates the largest constellation of imaging satellites in history. This constellation delivers an unprecedented dataset of empirical information via a revolutionary cloud-based platform to authoritative figures in commercial, environmental, and humanitarian sectors. We are both a space company and data company all rolled into one.

Customers and users across the globe use Planet's data to develop new technologies, drive revenue, power research, and solve our world’s toughest obstacles.

Company overview:

TraceLink is the world’s largest Agentic Business Network, enabling life sciences and healthcare companies to build and manage a scalable digital workforce of governed, no-code AI agents that execute and coordinate mission-critical supply chain operations alongside human teams. Powered by the Integrate-Once™ OPUS platform, TraceLink links more than 300,000 network participants, enabling multi-enterprise processes at global scale.

Founded in 2009 with the simple mission of protecting patients, today Tracelink has 5 global offices, over 800 employees and more than 1700 customers in over 60 countries around the world. Our expanding product suite continues to protect patients and now also enhances multi-enterprise collaboration through innovative new applications such as MINT.

Tracelink is recognized as an industry leader by Gartner and IDC, and for having a great company culture by Comparably.

TraceLink is building an Agentic Supply Chain Operating System. Powered by the OPUS Platform, it continuously unifies the information required to perform operational work across multiple enterprises. It is built from the bottom up, starting with the companies that make up each customer's supply network.
The operating system rests on four foundations:
- Supply Network Digital Twin. A live representation of the partners, products, locations, and business transactions across the supply network, built on the Integrate-Once™ Agentic Business Network.
- Multienterprise Business Processes. Orders, shipments, inventory, quality, and compliance work that forms, adapts, and completes across enterprise boundaries rather than inside one system.
- Agentic Supply Chain Intelligence. Control Towers apply knowledge, analytics, and supply chain meta-reasoning to operational context, so people understand what is happening and what should happen next.
- Governed Agents. OPUS Agents are created as governed users, assigned to human managers, and controlled through OPUS Agent Profiles, roles, permissions, objectives, Tasks, Decisions, and Rules.
At the center of these foundations is the OPUS Brain: the cognitive layer that lets OPUS Agents perceive what is happening across the supply network, reason about it, plan, decide, coordinate with other agents and people, and learn from outcomes. All of this happens within the governance boundaries each agent is assigned. The OPUS Brain is what turns a governed identity into a capable digital teammate. Agents are users. Each has an identity, an assigned role, and scoped permissions, and every action it takes is recorded. The OPUS Brain makes sure every thought that leads to an action can be traced and explained as well.

The future of aerospace and defense starts here.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

The journey to space starts with the engines.

Ursa Major is bringing a new model to propulsion and defense technology: one where performance and access are no longer constrained by legacy systems. We design, build, and deploy advanced propulsion systems that power national security missions, hypersonic capabilities, and the future of space access.

Our mission requires an extraordinary team—one that will mold tomorrow’s critical technologies while deploying today’s best. We are an intrinsically motivated team with a passion for solving complex technical problems and empowering each other every day, knowing that there is always room for growth.

About The Role

Reporting directly to the Head of Digital Operations, the Director of Enterprise Systems & Software (ESS) is a strategic executive technology leader responsible for establishing central ownership, governance, and architectural rigor across Ursa Major's entire internal enterprise digital landscape.

This role officially transitions core enterprise system ownership out of legacy, ad-hoc structures (previously managed under Digital Manufacturing) and establishes a dedicated department built on extreme system ownership. You will lead a high-performing team of dedicated Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) across core enterprise platforms (PLM, ERP, MES, Data/BI) alongside our internal Software Engineering organization (which builds custom internal web applications, including our engine testing solution and enterprise integration middleware). Day 1 leadership scope includes inheriting an established team (1x Product Owner, 2x Senior Software Developers, and a Manager of Digital Manufacturing transitioning to lead Enterprise Systems Integrations) alongside hiring dedicated Systems Engineers/Architects across PLM (Windchill), ERP (Odoo), MES (Critical Manufacturing), Atlassian, and Data Science/Analytics.

As Ursa Major scales from 380 to 500+ employees and prepares for public-company operations, you will lead the evolution of our ERP (Odoo) into a public-company-ready platform. Over time, your organization will systematically absorb and professionalize adjacent business-critical systems—such as HighQA, Jama, Ignition, and Atlassian—building an integrated digital thread across ISA-95 levels and laying the technical foundation for a fully operational Digital Twin across our manufacturing facilities by EOY 2027.

Responsibilities:
- Establish centralized ownership and serve as the executive authority for all business-critical enterprise platforms, enforcing to internal stakeholders that ESS provides dedicated SME ownership, administration, and support.

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.

About the Role

This role leads the Business Systems Product team in the CIO organization.

Verkada runs on four value streams — Quote-to-Cash, Attract-to-Hire-to-Retire, Procure-to-Pay, and Record-to-Report. The systems behind them decide how fast the company can sell, hire, source, ship, and close the books. You own the product functions across them.

The portfolio spans both sides of the company. Some of these systems face partners and customers, where the experience is part of how Verkada competes and where the ambition is to be the easiest company in the industry to do business with. Others face employees, where the experience drives how the company scales. The bar is the same on both sides: systems people choose to use, intuitive enough to need almost no training, and scalable so overall company growth exceeds the rate of headcount growth.

Your team is organized by the functions it serves: Partner Ecosystem (Partner Portal and vStore), Finance, Supply Chain & Operations, Legal, and People. Each product manager owns the systems roadmap for their function and acts as the product counterpart to that function's leadership. You own the whole — including the parts that only work when someone connects them. A partner order has to land cleanly in NetSuite. A headcount plan has to reconcile between Workday and the financial model.

This is a fully onsite role in our San Mateo HQ

What You'll Do
- Build streamlined features for pricing configurations, automated approvals, checkout, payments, and fund requests (MDF/JSF) to enable partners to operate without manual intervention.
- Recruit and coach 6–10 PMs to write strong requirements, manage roadmaps, and serve as strategic partners to business leaders.

Via is a global leader in smart transportation, using technology to revolutionize mobility worldwide. Our impact ranges from transforming individual daily commutes to reducing the collective environmental cost of transit systems. We're driven by ambitious goals. This is an opportunity to join a core team reshaping how public mobility operates at scale.

We are looking for a Head of AI Research Product to lead the intersection of applied machine learning research and product innovation across Via's rider and transit operations platform. This role sits at the frontier of what AI can do for public transportation, not as a feature layer, but as the engine that makes the system smarter, more equitable, and more efficient for every rider and agency we serve.

This is a three-part role: innovating with lighthouse customers to pilot and pressure-test cutting-edge approaches in real-world transit environments, conducting original applied research, and driving productization of proven methods into Via's core platform.

What you'll do:
- Build and lead Via's AI research product function, defining the roadmap for how machine learning advances rider experience and transit network performance.
- Design and deploy reinforcement learning systems that optimize routing, pooling efficiency, and real-time dispatching, balancing rider satisfaction against vehicle utilization and transit agency cost targets.
- Pioneer AlphaGo-style machine learning for transit: combine deep reinforcement learning, and tree search over high-fidelity simulations of real transit networks, training policy and value networks that discover dispatching, pooling, and network-design strategies beyond what hand-built heuristics or conventional optimization can reach.
- Develop weighted ensemble models and multi-objective optimization frameworks that surface the right tradeoffs between competing system goals: wait times, cost per ride, emissions, and equity of service.
- Invent personalization systems that adapt the rider mobile experience in real time, surfacing relevant trip options, proactive alerts, and dynamic pricing signals, in close partnership with the rider mobile product team.
- Research and productize behavioral incentive models that increase ridership and shift demand to improve aggregation: surge smoothing mechanisms, loyalty structures, and gamified engagement grounded in behavioral economics and causal inference.
- Partner with lighthouse transit agencies to co-develop and validate novel AI approaches, turning field pilots into scalable platform features.
- Establish rigorous experimentation infrastructure (A/B testing, contextual bandits, offline policy evaluation) to measure the real-world impact of model changes on rider behavior and agency outcomes.

What we are looking for:
- MS or PhD in a quantitative field: machine learning, operations research, statistics, applied mathematics, or a related discipline.
- Deep hands-on proficiency in ML: reinforcement learning, supervised

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority whose mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid. NERC develops and enforces Reliability Standards; annually assesses seasonal and long‐term reliability; monitors the bulk power system through system awareness; and educates, trains, and certifies industry personnel. NERC’s area of responsibility spans the continental United States, Canada, and the northern portion of Baja California, Mexico. NERC is the Electric Reliability Organization (ERO) for North America, subject to oversight by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and provincial authorities in Canada. NERC’s jurisdiction includes users, owners, and operators of the bulk power system, which serves nearly 400 million people.

Our Mission

The vision for the ERO Enterprise, which is comprised of NERC and the six Regional Entities, is a highly reliable and secure North American bulk power system. Our mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid.

The Director leads multidisciplinary teams of engineers, analysts, data scientists, and technology professionals. The Director also works across the ERO Enterprise to advance consistent, technically rigorous, and increasingly sophisticated approaches to reliability assessment and performance analysis. Convene Hospitality Group (CHG) operates a global portfolio of lifestyle brands focused on creating places and experiences that bring people together. The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well.

If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team.
Director, Cloud Infrastructure

We're hiring a Director of Cloud Infrastructure to join Convene Hospitality Group's (CHG) Technology organization. It's a hands-on role with an AI-native mindset. There are no direct reports today. You’ll lead through the platform, redesigning how we deploy and setting the standards our product and corporate engineering teams build on. You'll also run the cloud, AI, and venue infrastructure under our portfolio of brands, from client-facing experiences to the systems that keep our nearly 40 venues running.

This is a rebuild. You design it and you build it.

Today, deployments are manual and happen about once a sprint. That's the starting line. You'll rethink how we ship so that deployments are unlocked, safe, secure, and governed.

You'll have high autonomy and real decision-making power over the tools we use and how we build. We're committed to AWS and will build deeply on it. Most of what sits on top is fair game: CI tooling, pipeline design, orchestration patterns, and source control. A decision like Bitbucket versus Git Hub is a live call, and it's yours to make.

Legacy migration follows the decisions. You make the call, then you do the move. This role will have a lot of influence.

This is a wide seat. You’ll work across product and corporate engineering, and you’re a big part of how we get to AI-first, spec-driven development.
What You’ll Do:
• Rebuild the deployment path. Own CI/CD end to end: build, release, and rollback. Take us from manual deploys to an automated path.
• Make it safe, secure and governed. Access control, audit trails, secrets management, environment separation, and a rollback path any engineer can execute.
• Make the platform calls. Source control, CI tooling, orchestration, and infrastructure-as-code patterns. Jenkins is what we run today; what we run next is up to you. Decide, document the trade-off, then go forth and migrate.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Rafay is seeking a hands-on Director of Technical Program Management to lead strategic customer deployments and drive execution across Rafay’s Kubernetes and GPU PaaS platform initiatives. This is a highly visible leadership role responsible for overseeing complex enterprise implementations while remaining deeply engaged in technical delivery, customer architecture discussions, and cross-functional execution.

The ideal candidate combines strong program leadership with deep technical expertise in Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, GPU/AI workloads, and enterprise platform delivery. This leader will serve as a trusted advisor to customers and internal stakeholders, helping drive successful onboarding, modernization, migration, and adoption initiatives across large-scale enterprise environments.

Unlike a traditional people-management-only director role, this position requires hands-on involvement in technical project execution, customer solutioning, escalation management, and operational leadership.

• Proven leadership managing complex enterprise technical programs and customer-facing implementations in cloud, Kubernetes, AI/ML, or infrastructure environments.
• Deep technical expertise in Kubernetes, GPU workloads, cloud platforms, containers, and modern infrastructure architectures.
• Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence customer leadership, engineering teams, and cross-functional partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES
• Lead and oversee strategic customer implementations for Rafay’s Kubernetes and GPU PaaS platform offerings.
• Serve as the primary technical program leader for large-scale onboarding, migration, modernization, and platform adoption initiatives.
• Drive program execution across multiple concurrent enterprise engagements while maintaining hands-on involvement in technical planning and delivery.
• Partner directly with customer engineering, platform, infrastructure, DevOps, and executive stakeholders to define scope, align priorities, and ensure successful outcomes.
• Lead customer discovery workshops, architecture reviews, technical planning sessions, and implementation governance.
• Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, Pre-Sales, and Partner teams to align delivery priorities and remove execution blockers.
• Provide technical leadership and guidance around Kubernetes, GPU infrastructure, cloud-native architectures, AI/ML platform deployments, hybrid cloud, and multi-cloud implementations.
• Establish scalable delivery processes, implementation methodologies, operational best practices, and program governance frameworks.
• Own program risk management, escalation handling, dependency tracking, and executive-level communication throughout the delivery lifecycle.

Subcritical Systems, Inc. is a venture-backed startup in Austin, Texas building the accelerator driven systems and the only US commercial manufacturer of accelerator cavities. About Tutor
We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Hardware Engineering to lead the team that designs and builds our robots. Mechanical, electrical, firmware and embedded, and manufacturing engineering all report to this role. You set the hardware roadmap with the CTO, you grow the team, and you are responsible for every robot we ship working as designed and building at the rate we need. You report to the CTO.
The hardware organization will grow a lot, in people and in the range of products it covers. The person in this role builds the teams that make that happen, hires the people who lead them, and keeps the whole thing running well as it gets bigger.

Requirements
- You have led and grown a hardware engineering organization to 50 or more people, and shipped a complex electromechanical product in volume through it
- You have led mechanical, electrical, and firmware or embedded engineers, and can hire and judge all three
- You have owned manufacturing engineering, or worked closely enough with it to build that team: process, test, fixtures, and design for manufacturing
- You have developed the managers who lead teams under you
- You have worked closely with a technical founder or CTO
Nice to haves
- Robotics, actuators, or motion control
- Leading engineers in more than one country
- Taking a product from first prototype to producti

sitemap:at&t:102055599776.description:
This is a full-time onsite role based in the location(s) posted and is performed from the designated work location five days per week. No relocation is offered.

AT&T's Chief Security Office is seeking an experienced cybersecurity leader to direct the strategy, architecture, governance, and operational effectiveness of the company's enterprise network security program. This position is accountable for the design, governance, and continuous improvement of enterprise firewall architecture, network segmentation strategy, intrusion detection and prevention capabilities (IDS/IPS), and other critical security controls that protect AT&T's infrastructure, applications, data, and services.

The Director leads multiple cybersecurity functions responsible for enterprise firewall governance, security architecture, segmentation programs, perimeter defense, threat detection and prevention, compliance, security engineering, and modernization initiatives. This role partners across technology and business organizations to reduce cyber risk, improve operational efficiency, and enable secure business transformation.

Key Responsibilities and Required Qualifications
- Leads enterprise firewall strategy, architecture, lifecycle management, governance, policy standards, rule management, and access controls.
- Modernizes firewall platforms through simplification, automation, scalability, compliance, technical debt reduction, and attack-surface minimization.
- Defines enterprise network segmentation and micro-segmentation strategies that protect critical assets and reduce lateral movement.
- Develops long-term network security architecture roadmaps with infrastructure, cloud, and application teams, balancing risk reduction and business enablement.
- Provides executive leadership for IDS/IPS, detection engineering, threat prevention, monitoring, analytics, continuous tuning, and incident readiness.
- Advances scalable security engineering through automation, orchestration, analytics, AI-enabled capabilities, policy automation, and workflow optimization.
- Establishes governance, audit readiness, executive metrics, dashboards, objectives, and performance indicators that demonstrate measurable risk reduction.
- Leads and develop high-performing cybersecurity teams, set priorities, build future leaders, and influence executive investment and risk decisions.
- Brings 10+ years of cybersecurity or network security experience, including 5+ years leading enterprise-scale programs or engineering teams in complex, regulated environments.
- Demonstrates deep expertise in enterprise firewalls, network segmentation, IDS/IPS, access governance, network and cloud security architecture, threat modeling, secure design, monitoring, and cybersecurity frameworks.

Education/Experience:
- Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field with 10+ years of related experience.

Preferred Qualifications
- CISSP, CISM, CCSP, GIAC, or equivale

Citi's Integrated Digital Assets Platform (CIDAP) is at the vanguard of institutional blockchain adoption — and security is its foundation. - Lead the end-to-end delivery of critical payment applications as a Senior Engineering Lead, owning the full software development lifecycle from architectural design through to production deployment and ongoing support.
- Design and build high-throughput, low-latency microservices using Java 8+, Spring Boot, and cloud-native principles, ensuring each service meets rigorous standards for performance, scalability, and security.
- Champion modern architectural patterns — including Domain-Driven Design, event-driven architecture, and containerization with Docker and Kubernetes — to accelerate the transformation of legacy payment platforms.

Join Controls Technology division as a Technology Product Owner. In this critical role, you will act as the bridge between complex business needs and our engineering teams. About San Francisco Public Library
The San Francisco Public Library (SFPL) connects our diverse communities to learning, opportunities, and each other. The library system includes the architecturally significant Main Library, an anchor institution in the city's Civic Center, 27 neighborhood branch libraries that serve all neighborhoods throughout the city, two administrative buildings and four bookmobiles. With a collection of more than 5 million items, and circulation exceeding 14.5 million each year, SFPL serves more than 4.5 million visitors annually.
The library embraces its role as the most democratic of institutions, providing safe and welcoming facilities for all. Through a robust array of services and programs, the library is dedicated to advancing literacy and learning, serving as a cultural amplifier, acting as a catalyst for community engagement, guiding patrons as a thoughtful navigator, and providing essential resources to support healthy, equitable communities. SFPL must build a culture, space and workplace that is accessible and welcoming to all current and future employees and to actively build an environment in which all people regardless of background, identity, or ability, can be equal participants. Organizations everywhere struggle under the crushing costs and complexities of “solutions” that promise to simplify their lives. To create a better experience for their customers and employees. To help them grow. Software is a choice that can make or break a business. Create better or worse experiences. Propel or throttle growth. Business software has become a blocker instead of ways to get work done.
There’s another option. Freshworks. With a fresh vision for how the world works.
Freshworks Inc. builds uncomplicated service software that delivers exceptional employee and customer experiences. Our people-first approach to AI eliminates friction, helping businesses reduce complexity, lower cost-to-serve, and deliver faster, more human support through enterprise-grade yet easy-to-use CX and IT solutions. Nearly 75,000 companies, including Bridgestone, New Balance, Nucor, S&P Global, and Sony Music, trust Freshworks to power their Employee Experience (EX) and Customer Experience (CX) operations.
Fresh vision. Real impact. Come build it with us.

We're looking for a Director, Digital Experience to lead how customers discover, evaluate, and engage with Freshworks through our website. You'll shape the web experience roadmap, lead designers and program managers, and partner with engineering to deliver better customer journeys and measurable business results.
You're a program manager at heart who stays close to the execution. You'll run Scrum across design and engineering, turn competing priorities into clear plans, and help the team deliver with speed and quality. You'll treat the website as a product, balancing launches and publishing needs with continuous improvements to its effectiveness.

What You'll Do

Web Experience and Roadmap
- Set the web roadmap and decide what to tackle next. Use customer needs and performance data to weigh improvements, redesigns, migrations, and localized experiences.
- Review designs with content and engineering partners. Make sure pages are easy to use and reflect the brand, with accessibility and conversion considered during design.
- Agree on web priorities with Web Revenue, Product Marketing, Demand Generation, and Marketing Operations. Turn campaign and product plans into work the team can deliver.

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.
Why join the Harvard Radcliffe Institute?
The Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University, known colloquially as Harvard Radcliffe Institute, is one of the world’s leading centers for interdisciplinary exploration. We bring together students, scholars, artists, and practitioners to pursue curiosity-driven research, expand human understanding, and grapple with questions that demand insight from across disciplines.
The Fellowship Program annually supports the work of 50 leading artists and scholars. Academic Ventures fosters collaborative research projects and sponsors lectures and conferences that engage scholars with the public. The Schlesinger Library documents the lives of American women of the past and present for the future, furthering the Institute's commitment to women, gender, and society. The Emerging Leaders Program is a youth leadership development program partnering local high school sophomores with Harvard undergraduates in a mentoring relationship.
The Institute’s work is shaped by its history as the former Radcliffe College—a school founded to ensure that the standard of education embodied in Harvard was accessible to women, who were then excluded from the University. But the legacy of Radcliffe College is not simply coeducation at Harvard; it is the recognition that universities will always be greater when they draw wisdom and talent from the widest possible pool.
Take a look at this video to get different staff perspectives on working at Harvard Radcliffe Institute !

Reporting to the Library’s Executive Director, the Head of Technical Services will set and guide the department’s strategic direction, advancing effective, forward-looking approaches to technical services that enhance discovery and ensure timely, user-centered access to the Library’s holdings. You set the strategy that makes their roadmaps resolve into a single lifecycle rather than four products that ship past each other.

The Developer Reach feature area alone unlocks a path to building in production that admins can manage at scale without losing control, and it demands real technical depth to steer. You will also carry a broad surface, over twenty product areas, with the escalation volume that comes with it, and you will need to run that operational load without letting it consume the strategic work.

Veolia Group is a global leader in environmental services, operating across all five continents with nearly 218,000 employees. Specializing in water, energy, and waste management, Veolia Group designs and implements innovative solutions for decarbonization, depollution, and resource regeneration, supporting communities and industries in their ecological transformation. Within this framework, Veolia's Water Technology Business brings together a dedicated team of experienced professionals committed to tackling the world’s most complex challenges related to water scarcity, quality, productivity, and energy. Together, we pursue a shared mission to create a more sustainable future.

Veolia Water Tech is a worldwide leader in water recovery, treatment, and reuse. We design and supply a range of water systems, from food and beverage applications, to municipal water, to microelectronics ultrapure water and heavy industrial wastewater treatment. We serve more than 50,000 customers worldwide and treat more than 11 million cubic meters of water every day. We simply aim to be the benchmark company for ecological transformation across the world.
At Veolia Water Tech, we realise diverse teams make smarter decisions, deliver better results, and build stronger communities. We are an organisation that champions diversity and inclusion at every rung of the ladder and are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We offer challenging and meaningful careers, with competitive benefits and flexible work arrangements.
SUMMARY OF THE JOB

The Senior Director of Process Engineering provides strategic and operational leadership for the WaterTech NORAM process engineering function focused on the design and development of water, wastewater and biosolid treatment systems. This executive leader is accountable to all the Business Line Leaders and the NORAM Regional Leader for building and leading high-performing teams of process engineering experts, ensuring the

delivery of technically sound, commercially aligned, and operationally executable solutions across multiple industry markets.
This role is responsible for advancing engineering excellence through a balanced focus on accuracy, speed, standardization, innovation, and market responsiveness. The Senior Director will shape engineering strategy, optimize organizational capability, and drive alignment between process engineering, commercial objectives, customer needs, and long-term business growth.
The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in water, wastewater and biosolid treatment, strong people leadership, and the ability to translate market requirements into scalable process solutions that enhance our competitive advantage.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership
- Lead the vision, strategy, and execution of the process engineering function in support of Water Tech NORAM integrated growth objectives.
- Establish engineering priorities, operating models, and capability plans that enable the business to respond effect

We are seeking an experienced and visionary  Director Application Security  to lead the strategy, development, and execution of our Application Security program. Reporting to the Vice President of Security Operations, this leader will be responsible for maturing and optimizing application security capabilities across the software development lifecycle, ensuring secure-by-design principles are embedded into engineering practices while enabling rapid delivery of innovative products.

This individual will partner closely with Engineering, Product Management, Architecture, DevOps, Cloud Engineering, and Security Operations to integrate security into every phase of software development. The successful candidate will have extensive experience building or transforming Application Security programs within complex technology organizations and will possess the ability to influence engineering culture through collaboration rather than gatekeeping.

Role Responsibilities:
Application Security Strategy
- Develop and execute the enterprise Application Security strategy aligned with business and technology objectives.
- Build and mature a scalable Application Security program supporting modern software development practices.
- Define the long-term roadmap for secure software development across cloud, web, mobile, APIs, and emerging technologies.
- Establish secure-by-design principles and integrate them throughout the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).

Secure Development Lifecycle (SSDLC)
- Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of a Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC).
- Develop standards and security requirements for application development.
- Partner with engineering teams to integrate security early within CI/CD pipelines.
- Promote developer-friendly security practices that minimize friction while improving software security.

Security Testing & Assurance
Oversee enterprise application security testing, including:
- Static Application Security Testing (SAST)
- Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST)
- Software Composition Analysis (SCA)
- Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST)
- API Security Testing
- Container Security
- Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) Security
- Secure code reviews
- Penetration testing coordination

DevSecOps Enablement
- Partner with DevOps teams to embed automated security controls into CI/CD pipelines.
- Improve automation of security testing and vulnerability management.
- Reduce developer burden through integrated tooling and streamlined workflows.
- Measure security effectiveness while enabling engineering velocity.

Operationalize Continuous Threat & Exposure Management (CTEM) across critical applications and business services

The Opportunity

Adobe's Digital Video & Audio (DVA) business builds Premiere Pro, After Effects, and Media Encoder, the tools that filmmakers, broadcasters, and creators trust to tell their stories. At the center of these products sits the Realtime Experience (RTX) team. RTX owns the rendering engine, GPU abstraction layer, compositor, video player, importer and exporter host, and Effects and Transitions SDK. Every frame our customers play, edit, and export passes through this stack.

The next 12 months will define the future of video creation at Adobe. RTX is finishing its GPU-first pipeline, moving to a modern graphics API, and designing how AI-native rendering fits in. Leader for this team will shape the engine under Premiere Pro and After Effects for years to come.

We are hiring a Director of Engineering for RTX. The team is senior and highly specialized, and it needs a leader with matching depth. The Director will own these modernization efforts and align the many teams that touch rendering, as Topaz and LTX integrations arrive.

What You Will Do

This role sets the technical vision for the rendering technology behind DVA's desktop products, with a near-term focus on Premiere Pro performance and stability. Architectural decisions come with clear investment plans for engineering and quality engineering.
- Deliver the GPU-first rendering pipeline to improve playback, scrubbing, and dropped frames.
- Choose and lead the move to a modern graphics and compute API such as DirectX 12, Vulkan, or Dawn/WebGPU.
- Define how AI features and partner technologies such as Topaz and LTX fit the render pipeline while keeping quality and user experience high.
- Unify rendering, effects, and transitions across desktop, web, and mobile.
- Build lasting partnerships with technology leaders and shape our roadmap around their platform plans.
- Work with media and format teams to modernize legacy components, and align partner teams on shared priorities.
- Lead the engineering side of a Developer Relations effort to unify and document our SDKs and raise third-party plugin quality, protecting a key competitive advantage.

The Director also grows a team of managers, architects, and senior engineers, protects the quality bar, and coaches leaders as the organization changes.

What We Are Looking For (Must Have)

- Partner with Product Marketing, Design, Test, and Package Development teams to define product requirements and specifications
- Own technical risk identification and mitigation planning across the team's deliverables
- Drive schedule adherence for architecture reviews, tape-out readiness, and testchip milestones
- Represent the team in program reviews, providing status, risks, and technical recommendations to senior management

Process & Quality
- Establish and improve design review processes across Systems, Firmware, Package, and Magnetics
- Ensure design decisions are well-documented and traceable (specs, simulation results, test data)
- Promote reuse of proven architectures, IP blocks, and magnetics solutions across projects

Required Qualifications
- MS/PhD in Electrical

Overview
The Senior Director, IT Service Operations owns the IT Service Operations pillar: Technical Support, Networks, Asset and Fleet Management, Account Management and identity provisioning, and Service Delivery. This role is the operational command layer that translates strategy into daily execution, holds the pillar accountable to published standards, and builds the operating model that lets managers manage and engineers engineer without constant escalation. This is a people leadership and operational management role, not a technical architect or engineer role. You will set the standards, evaluate work against them, and hold engineers accountable to them. The ASPCA is the nation's largest humane society and one of the world's leading animal welfare organizations. Our mission is to provide effective means for the prevention of cruelty to animals throughout the United States. The Information Technology division supports approximately 1,400 employees across New York City headquarters, shelters, clinics, mobile rescue units, and field operations nationwide.
This is an opportunity to lead a transformation as the pillar is in active growth and we are looking for someone to establish practices where none exist, retire workarounds that have become load-bearing, and shepherd a shift toward structured, repeatable operations through coaching and collaboration rather than mandate. The candidate who will thrive here wants to build, is energized by ambiguity and challenge, and is driven by our mission.

- The Sr. Director, IT Service Operations reports directly to the VP, Technology Services and has 4-6 direct and matrixed reports, with approximately 15 indirect reports. AI Driven Radio Access Networks Director The Opportunity:
The Director of AI Driven Radio Access Networks (AI RAN) Product Engineering is a senior leadership role responsible for defining, building, and executing the organization’s strategy for applying artificial intelligence and machine learning to modern Radio Access Networks. This leader oversees innovation, architecture, and product development—advancing our product baseline and incorporating new innovations related to AI, sensing, and communications.

This role collaborates closely with product management, customer delivery, and market teams as well as external ecosystem partners such as vendors, standards bodies, and research institutions. Due to the nature of work performed within this facility, U.S. citizenship is required.

What You'll Work On:
- Develop and own the AI RAN product and innovation roadmap.
- Identify opportunities for product and solution differentiation to include those related to sensing, integrations of open weight models for optimized communications, and development, or integration of new RU products.
- Represent the AI RAN function in executive forums and industry collaborations.
- Lead the design and evolution of AI enhanced RAN architectures with a focus on developing new “AI for RAN” applications and innovations.
- Ensure alignment with 3GPP, O RAN Alliance, and other relevant industry standards.
- Partner with the security team to adopt new functionality and security baselines, incorporating new features related to secure AI.
- Work with Agentic and Physical AI teams to develop and host new Edge AI applications and workloads.
- Apply new agentic based applications to operate, secure, and optimize the AI-RAN network.
- Collaborate with procurement and vendor management to influence ODM vendor roadmaps and strategies in accordance with the roadmap and product release strategy.
- Work with customer delivery teams to successfully deploy and integrate the product and solution into customer environments.
- Establish KPIs and benchmarking frameworks to quantify performance, cost efficiency, and customer impact.

- Champion a culture of continuous innovation within the organization.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

- Experience with AI/ML systems and their applicability to wireless networks
- Experience leading large cross-functional teams and delivering wireless, satellite, or network solutions in the market
- Knowledge of O RAN and AI-RAN
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or Computer Engineering

Nice If You Have:
- Experience deploying AI/ML in telco or mission‑critical environments
- Experience with network automation frameworks, including SON or intent‑based networking
- Experience in standards

The Vice President of Technology provides strategic leadership for Biltmore's enterprise technology, digital guest experience, data capabilities, and artificial intelligence initiatives. About this role

Data Product Owner, Vice President – XFT

Your team
BlackRock’s Cross-Functional Technology (XFT) team brings together people, process, data and technology to establish scalable, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled platforms and the technology foundation supporting the firm’s long-term growth strategy. XFT enables a unified, AI-first enterprise focused on simplifying decision-making and increasing operational leverage.

Your role and impact
As a Data Product Owner, you will own a portfolio of data products supporting BlackRock’s corporate functions, guiding products from discovery and definition through delivery, adoption and ongoing evolution. The role combines hands-on product ownership with enterprise data expertise, translating complex business needs into reusable, governed data products; shaping domain data models, semantic constructs and enterprise definitions; and driving execution across stakeholder and technology teams. You may direct the work of a small group of analysts and other contributors while remaining actively involved in product definition, analysis and delivery.

Your responsibilities
In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:
- Own assigned domain data products from discovery through roadmap, requirements, delivery, adoption, measurement and lifecycle management.
- Represent products through Agile planning and delivery, driving decisions, dependencies, prioritization and execution through completion.
- Lead product discovery and requirements analysis, evaluating business value, cost, dependencies and competing priorities to recommend appropriate sequencing and tradeoffs.
- Partner with business stakeholders to establish clear product outcomes, data definitions, service expectations and measures of success.
- Design and evolve domain data models, including core business concepts, relationships, reference and master data, and reusable data structures.
- Partner closely with data engineering, platform, business intelligence (BI), reporting and architecture teams on pipelines, transformations, access patterns, entitlements, analytical consumption and distribution mechanisms.
- Provide product direction and day-to-day leadership to small analyst teams.

Company:
The Boeing Company

The Boeing Company is looking for a Software Chief Architect - AvionX to join the AvionX Software team located in Long Beach, California . This position will focus on leading the AvionX Software Engineering organization.

The Chief Software Architect for AvionX Software Vertical is the highest software technical authority across airborne software programs from architecture definition through certification closure. This role owns the coherence, integrity, and DO-178C/LOR compliance posture of software architectures across commercial and defense platforms, bridging software engineering discipline with system-level safety objectives and regulatory strategy. - Oversees analyses, monitoring and improvement of the efficiency and stability of embedded software systems
- Oversees tracking and evaluation of internal and supplier software team performance to ensure product and process compliance to project plans and industry standards
- Provides consultation on integration of embedded software with hardware components
- Provides technical leadership for embedded software project management functions

- Bachelor's degree
- This position requires the ability to obtain a US Security Clearance for which the US Government requires US Citizenship

- 5+ years of experience with embedded software development, verification, or certification

- 3+ years of experience using Matlab/Simulink

The Head of Infrastructure Standards & Operational Management is a senior technology leader responsible for establishing the standards, governance, programs, asset discipline, and financial transparency that enable a scalable, resilient, and cost-effective global infrastructure environment.
