Who is NTE, NTE 35W, and LBJ?

The North Tarrant Express (NTE) was the first design-build-finance-operate-maintain managed lanes project in Texas and consisted of the complete reconstruction of 13.3 miles of the existing I-820/SH-183 corridor between Dallas and Fort Worth. Since opening in October 2014, nine months ahead of the contracted completion date, the general highway lanes are experiencing a 70% decrease in congestion time and a 15% increase in average speed. This Cintra-led project has doubled capacity and significantly improved mobility along this heavily congested corridor that traverses the heart of six cities through Northeast Tarrant County.

The North Tarrant Express 35W (NTE 35W) project spans 16.8 miles from I-30 in downtown Fort Worth to Eagle Parkway at the north end of Alliance Airport. The project is operated and maintained by the Cintra-led consortium in North Texas. This project has improved mobility by adding additional road capacity through a combination of general highway lanes and continuous frontage roads, along with tolled express lanes that use variable pricing to keep traffic moving.

The LBJ Express (LBJ) is currently the largest P3 operation in Texas and one of the largest ever undertaken in the U.S. It is a regionally-significant transportation improvement project in North Texas that is relieving severe congestion in the dense urban area of north Dallas. In 2009, the Cintra-led consortium was selected to complete the design, construction, finance, operation, and maintenance of the project along I-635 and I-35E. Since opening in September 2015, the general highway lanes are realizing a 60% decrease in congestion time and a 10% increase in average speed.

At Corebridge Financial, we believe action is everything. That’s why every day we partner with financial professionals and institutions to make it possible for more people to take action in their financial lives, for today and tomorrow.

The Information Technology (IT) organization is the technological foundation of our business and works in collaboration with our partners from across the company. The Director of AI Security ensures that standard is backed by a rigorous, enforceable security layer — covering model risk, data protection, identity, vulnerability management, and attack-path/threat modeling across the AI lifecycle, from model selection and data sourcing through deployment, monitoring, and decommissioning.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can operate simultaneously at the standards/control-framework level (audit- and board-ready documentation) and the technical control level, while building a trusted, collaborative relationship with a peer team that owns adjacent AI governance.

Role Summary:
The Data Domain Owner will own and lead the strategic direction, prioritization, and governance for one of DaVita’s five enterprise data domains (Village). Domain Owners will be accountable for ensuring domain data provides substantial enterprise value (e.g., high-quality, accessible, compliant data that enables high-value Village use cases). The Domain Owner will coordinate closely with Data Stewards and Data Custodians across several ‘sub-domains’ (categories of data within the domain). These Data Stewards and Data Custodians will drive frontline execution (e.g., for data quality and accessibility) within a given sub-domain as part of a “two-in-a-box” model: The Data Steward will represent the “business user” perspective, while the Data Custodian will represent the “technical user” perspective.

Domain Owners will help Data Stewards and Data Custodians prioritize their efforts, working closely with business leaders across DaVita to ensure alignment with Village-wide priorities. Domain Owners will also drive Domain Working Groups to coordinate activity across different sub-domains (e.g., aligning consistent data definitions across different areas of the business).

Vice President, Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)

About DaVita
DaVita is a Fortune 500 healthcare community dedicated to transforming care and improving the lives of patients across the globe. As one of the nation's largest providers of kidney care services, our mission is to be the provider, partner, and employer of choice. We operate with a "Community First, Company Second" mindset, guided by our core values: Service Excellence, Integrity, Team, Continuous Improvement, Passion, Accountability, and Fulfillment.

Position Overview
DaVita is seeking a dynamic, strategic executive leader to serve as our Vice President, Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) .

Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer (CIO), the CISO is the principal executive responsible for DaVita’s global cybersecurity vision, information security operations, technical risk governance, and regulatory compliance. In this role, you will lead an enterprise-scale security organization dedicated to protecting sensitive patient data, clinical systems, proprietary intellectual property, and critical infrastructure across more than 2,800 dialysis centers and corporate environments nationwide.

The ideal leader brings deep technical acumen, modern architectural perspective (Zero Trust, Cloud Modernization, AI Governance), and executive presence to champion security as a business enabler and patient-safety imperative.

Key Responsibilities
Security Strategy, Vision & Architecture
- Formulate, articulate, and execute a multi-year enterprise cybersecurity and risk management strategy aligned with DaVita’s strategic business priorities and digital transformation initiatives.
- Drive architectural modernization across enterprise security systems, implementing Zero Trust principles, advanced Identity and Access Management (IAM), and resilient cloud security frameworks (AWS, Azure, and multi-tenant SaaS).
- Establish governance, risk assessments, and guardrails for emerging technologies, including Generative AI, machine learning pipelines, and connected biomedical/IoT devices.

- Partner with senior leaders across Underwriting, Claims, Finance, Operations, and Executive Management to identify priorities and deliver data-driven solutions that improve business outcomes.
- Own the Reinsurance data and analytics roadmap, translating business strategy into a prioritized portfolio of data, reporting, and analytics initiatives.
- Collaborate with Technology and Enterprise Data & Analytics teams to define requirements, prioritize investments, and deliver scalable data and analytics capabilities.
- Lead the development and continuous enhancement of operational, management, and executive reporting solutions, ensuring stakeholders have access to timely and actionable insights.
- Establish and oversee key performance indicators, scorecards, dashboards, and performance measurement frameworks, including governance of KPI

workday:first management:JR17266.description:
This job combines two things that usually sit with different people: owning products and building them. One product is a real-time tracking and communications app that hundreds of thousands of families and their school districts rely on, where a wrong notification reaches a parent waiting at a bus stop. The other is the technology behind a service for students with special transportation needs, students experiencing homelessness, and out-of-district students, delivered through contracted local transportation providers.
Each product has a Business Product Owner who owns its business outcomes, priorities, and commercial decisions. You are their partner on the IT side, owning how those priorities become software within the lines our product management operating model sets. It gets built in an agentic delivery framework owned by a senior technical team. You own its product side: the specs, acceptance criteria, and evals that go in, and the call on whether the result met the business need.
You also build. In traditional product management, requirements get written, handed to engineering, and interpreted somewhere along the way. Here, a conversation with a stakeholder can become working software in days, and the person who had the conversation is often the one directing the agents that build it. You should already be building with agents, even if it is not yet how you do all of your work. In this role, building stops being something you do alongside product management and becomes how you do it.
You will start with a small team, so expect to lead and build at the same time. The people you lead may come from more traditional roles, and helping them make the same shift is part of the job. You will also own the budget, vendor relationships, and contracts behind this work, AI tooling included.

How You'll Work
AI runs through your entire workflow, from discovery and specs to the build, tests, documentation, and reporting. We are looking for someone already working this way who can show what it has produced, not someone with a thesis on where AI is going.
Requirements here usually arrive as a conversation rather than a ticket, and you will often be the one having it. You will build inside a framework someone else runs, which means understanding a rule's reasoning before deciding it is in your way. You will be measured on whether what ships is correct and whether the business got what it actually needed, not on volume.

A typical week may include:
- Sitting with district staff, families, or the team that coordinates our transportation providers, then deciding with a Business Product Owner whether a problem belongs on the roadmap.
- Turning a conversation like that into a working prototype and using it to agree on requirements before the full build starts.
- Reviewing work with a team member who is still learning to build with agents, and explaining the reasoning behind your feedback.

To support our extraordinary teams who build great products and contribute to our growth, we’re looking to add a Sr. Director, Validation Test Engineering located in Austin, TX.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, the Sr. Director, Validation Test Engineering will establish and lead the OCTO validation, characterization, and qualification capability for SpinCo’s integrated data center platforms. This role will define validation strategies, test plans, acceptance criteria, lab capabilities, test data infrastructure, and development lifecycle gates for advanced power, advanced cooling, controls, and integrated platform products. The role ensures SpinCo ships integrated systems that work reliably at the rack, pod, and data-center levels.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be active in your own deliverables, personally shaping test strategies, test plans, and acceptance criteria, digging into test data, and standing up lab and test capability rather than only directing others to do so. We are looking for a leader who sets the technical bar by engaging directly in validation and data, and who is measured by the reliability of what we ship.

- Define validation strategies, test plans, test standards, and acceptance criteria for advanced power, advanced cooling, control systems, and integrated platform offerings.
- Stand up and operate test and characterization labs required to validate rack-level, pod-level, and platform-level performance and reliability.
- Gate products through development lifecycle milestones from concept to design/development, validation, production introduction, and release.
- Drive design verification testing, reliability testing, automated testing, regression testing, certification planning, and design-for-test requirements.
- Partner with manufacturing, quality, and BUs on production-readiness reviews, first-article inspections, ramp readiness, and factory test alignment.
- Build test data infrastructure that feeds back into design, predictive maintenance models, digital twins, qualification data, and complex controls systems.
- Engage directly with customers and partners to understand performance, reliability, interoperability, and qualification requirements for AI data center infrastructure.

The experience we’re looking to add to our team:
- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related technical discipline; advanced degree preferred or equivalent

Position Summary:
The Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine at Florida Atlantic University seeks an outstanding academic educator and clinician for the full-time faculty position of Director of Surgical Simulation and Technology for the Department of Surgery and the General Surgery Residency Program.

The Director of Surgical Simulation and Technology provides leadership for the development, and implementation of simulation-based surgical education programs within the Department of Surgery. This role is responsible for managing all required surgical simulation curricula and training programs, including ACGME and American Board of Surgery requirements, while ensuring surgery residents and medical students receive comprehensive training in open, laparoscopic, endoscopic, and robotic surgical techniques. The Director develops and implements competency-based assessment methods, coordinates team-based simulation activities and works closely with faculty to promote engagement in surgical education and skills training. This position will be structured with 35% clinical responsibilities and 65% administrative responsibilities.

As a core faculty member of the General Surgery Residency Program, the Director provides direct teaching, supervision, and mentorship to residents and students in clinical, simulation, and classroom settings. The position fosters a culture of academic excellence by supporting resident-led scholarly activity, research and quality improvement initiatives. The Director serves as a professional role model and career mentor while contributing to the educational mission of the College of Medicine. Clinical responsibilities include providing surgical care, clinical teaching, and supervision of residents and medical students in operative and patient care settings.

The Director also collaborates with university and hospital leadership to advance simulation technologies, secure funding, and expand educational capabilities throughout the system. Responsibilities include guiding the acquisition of advanced simulation equipment, supporting the development of an American College of Surgeons Accredited Education Institute (AEI), and ensuring that simulation resources serve both surgical trainees and practicing healthcare professionals. The position performs additional projects and responsibilities as assigned in support of the department's strategic goals.

The successful candidate will be an ABS board-certified surgeon with a demonstrated commitment to graduate medical education, surgical education, patient safety, quality improvement, and resident professional development. Job Description:
The Director for Service Infrastructure and Cybersecurity at Fluence is a pivotal technical leadership role responsible for governing our Tier 2 global infrastructure, platform operations, and information security ecosystem. Operating as the primary engineering and escalation authority for our Remote Monitoring and Diagnostic Center (RMDC / Tier 1), this position ensures the high availability, security, resilience, and scalable growth of Fluence’s enterprise cloud assets, central data platform infrastructure, and customer-facing edge environments.

In this role, you will lead high-performing technical practices spanning AWS cloud administration, Zero Trust cybersecurity, network and remote connectivity, platform firmware and operating systems, and automated deployment pipelines. You will collaborate closely with Field Service Engineers (FSEs), product engineering, and security compliance teams to drive continuous service improvement, uphold strict operational SLAs, and safeguard the mission-critical digital systems powering Fluence energy storage operations worldwide.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Infrastructure & Platform Operations (Tier 2 Lead)
- Oversee global AWS resource administration, including EC2 OS lifecycle updates, EBS snapshots, AMI management, S3 lifecycle policies, resource cleanup, and capacity/quota monitoring.
- Direct network architecture and operations, including global firewalls, Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), VPC routing, and secure VPN connectivity to customer sites and jump hosts.
- Administer Central Data Acquisition Systems (DAS - OS6 & OS7) and database infrastructures, driving MySQL/NoSQL automation, database performance tuning, shard rollover, patching, and data purge policies.
- Oversee platform lifecycle management across Linux OS, F.OS, firmware, controllers, servers, UPS devices, switches, routers, and firewalls.

Cybersecurity & Information Security Governance
- Champion identity and access management (IAM) governance across AWS and connected platforms, enforcing MFA, role-based policies, least privilege, key rotations, and periodic joiner/mover/leaver access reviews.

As a Sr Director - AI & Platform Engineering you are accountable for building and operating the enterprise agent platform that enables every team to safely develop, deploy, and scale AI agents across the organization. - Build and operate the trust and quality framework, including evaluations, observability, release gates, performance monitoring, and continuous improvement mechanisms for production agents
- Own platform security, governance, and operational excellence, including agent identity, authorization, policy enforcement, auditability, incident response, SLOs, and cost management

About Us
GFL Environmental Services Inc. ("GESI") is a high-growth environmental services company recently carved out of GFL Environmental Inc. Backed by leading private equity firms, GESI delivers liquid waste, industrial cleaning, and soil remediation services across North America through a vertically integrated platform of over 230 sites and a fleet of 1,800+ vehicles. Our employees, collectively known as 'Team Green,' enjoy numerous benefits: career advancement opportunities, competitive benefits, job stability within an essential services company, and the chance to make a positive impact every day for our customers and communities, Green for Life!

The National Director, Environment, Health & Safety (EH&S) - USA provides strategic, executive, and operational leadership over all EH&S programs across national operations, high-hazard facilities, field sites, and refinery operations. This role transforms regional EH&S achievements into national standards, establishing continuous improvement frameworks, driving a culture of safety excellence, and ensuring operational alignment with complex federal, provincial, and local regulatory requirements across USA and North America.

The National Director bridges enterprise strategy with operational reality: developing digital EH&S platforms, overseeing high-severity risk mitigation, leading incident management governance, and directing cross-functional teams to achieve an industry leading operating model.

- Formulate, govern, and continuously enhance the enterprise wide HS management system framework (KPIs, EH&SMS, Corporate Safety Standards, policies, and SOPs), establishing consistent safety standards.
- Foster a company-wide culture of safety excellence by driving executive-led safety initiatives, continuous training programs, and proactive risk mitigation strategies. Drive the standardization of safe operating practices, hazardous task controls, and engineering risk mitigations to protect personnel, assets, and operational continuity.
- Establish senior leadership oversight and executive reporting protocols for critical incidents, ensuring operational transparency, accountability, and continuous organizational learning.
- Align EH&S stewardship goals with business objectives to support overall operational sustainability, compliance, and long-term organizational success.
- Provide strategic direction and executive oversight for risk management across all operations and diverse client industrial sites
- Oversee HS onboarding, integrating acquired business units, personnel, and infrastructure into corporate EH&S management systems and safety cultures.
- Oversee comprehensive environmental compliance, facility monitoring, site remediation, and land-stewardship strategies.

JOB SUMMARY
STRATEGY & TRANSFORMATION OFFICE (STO)
Highmark Health is committed to fixing healthcare and solving the challenges facing our communities, such as improving individual health, increasing patient engagement, and making healthcare more affordable. The Strategy and Transformation Office is at the forefront of this mission, developing and executing innovative plans to achieve these goals through our Enterprise Strategy known as Living Health.

If you're a resilient, strategic thinker, a strong experienced problem-solver, you are eager to challenge the status quo, and you are passionate about creating a healthier future for all, consider joining the Enterprise Strategy and Transformation Office. You'll be an integral part of the leadership team dedicated to making Living Health a reality.

As part of the enterprise Strategy & Transformation Office, the incumbent will collaborate with the senior-most executives and stakeholders across the organization to assist in the development and improvement of key enterprise strategic initiatives and will work closely with STO VPs and EVP to set project, office, and team direction.

The Director largely is responsible for:
- Project leadership – lead a portfolio of strategy projects from end-to-end, including: scoping the project, developing workplans, staffing workstreams, leading problem solving and solutioning, developing materials, building client relationships, influencing leadership direction, and presenting results to executive leadership.
- People leadership – responsible for the development and growth of a small team of strategists, including ongoing performance management and mentorship.
- Office leadership – improving how we work as a team, creating actionable improvement plans, supporting general office management to ensure team effectiveness and satisfaction.

This position is based out of the Pittsburgh (or Buffalo) office with a minimum 3-day per week in-office requirement Tuesday through Thursday.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES
- Perform management responsibilities to include, but are not limited to: involved in hiring and termination decisions, coaching and development, rewards and recognition, performance management and staff productivity.

- Work with business / market owners to identify key business issues, apply right analytical framework, develop solution and recommendations, represent findings to stakeholders, and own the outcome.
- Manage major strategy projects with the help of internal or external strategy consulting resources.
- Supports Enterprise Strategy office in development of overall Enterprise Focus 5 strategy portfolio and cross-enterprise strategies as needed.
- Other duties as assigned or requested.

HHMI is focused on supporting and moving science forward in a variety of different ways ranging from conducting basic biomedical research, empowering educators, inspiring students, developing the next generation of scientists – even stretching into film and media production.  Our Headquarters is in the greater Washington, DC metro area and is home to over 300 employees with expertise in investments , communications, digital production, biomedical sciences, and everything in between.  The work housed here supports and augments the groundbreaking research conducted in HHMI labs across the nation.  As HHMI scientists continue to push boundaries in laboratories and classrooms, you can be sure that your contributions while working here are making a difference.

HHMI is a nonprofit scientific research organization that supports scientists and educators across the country. Finance and People & Culture run the processes that pay, hire, reimburse, and support all of them. Most of those legacy processes were built for a world before Workday was mature and before AI could do real work. That world is gone. HHMI is moving procurement and expense onto Workday and is putting AI tools in the hands of every employee through EverydayAI. The open question is what the processes themselves should look like, and that is what this role answers.

HHMI’s EverydayAI initiative is putting AI tools and agents into operations across the institute. You will not need to build the business case for AI or convince leadership it matters. That work is done. What you will do is decide where AI belongs in payroll and finance processes, partner with the EverydayAI and Technology teams to build and pilot the first agents and be honest about what works and what does not.

You start with payroll, and you own it. You lead the payroll team and are accountable for every cycle running accurately and on time across the three populations. At the same time, you take the function apart end to end and redesign it: Workday-native, with AI and agents doing the work they are good at and people doing the work that needs judgment. Then you implement it with your team. You do not need to arrive as a payroll expert. You do need to learn the operation, exercise sound judgment, and lead changes that preserve accurate, on-time pay, working with an experienced payroll manager.

Once payroll is running the new way, you carry the same method into the rest of Finance and People & Culture.

Summary:
The Technology Risk & Control Director – Cybersecurity is a senior front-line Technology Risk leader responsible for providing risk insight, advisory support, and effective challenge across cybersecurity and information protection domains.

The role works collaboratively with Cybersecurity and Technology leaders responsible for establishing and maintaining standards, procedures, controls, metrics, and operational practices. The Technology Risk Director does not replace or assume those ownership responsibilities. Instead, this role helps leaders understand risk exposure, evaluate the effectiveness and sustainability of the control environment, identify emerging or systemic risk themes, and make well-informed risk decisions.

The position will provide risk expertise across Identity and Access Management (IAM), Privileged Access Management (PAM), Data Protection, Cloud Security, Vulnerability and Exposure Management, Application Security, Security Architecture, Cybersecurity Operations, and other evolving cybersecurity domains.

The leader will bring strong cybersecurity and technology risk experience, sound judgment, and the ability to translate complex technical conditions into business risk, control implications, risk trends, and clear executive insights.

Duties and Responsibilities:
- Serve as a senior Technology Risk partner to Cybersecurity and Technology leadership, providing risk insight, advice, and constructive challenge across cybersecurity and information protection domains.
- Build strong, collaborative relationships with Cybersecurity, Technology, Data, business-aligned technology teams, Independent Risk, Compliance, Legal, Privacy, Audit, and other enterprise stakeholders.
- Provide risk insight across IAM, PAM, authentication and authorization, identity governance, Data Protection, Cloud Security, Vulnerability and Exposure Management, Application Security, Security Architecture, Cyber Operations, endpoint and network security, and cyber incident risk.
- Partner with Cybersecurity and Technology control owners to assess risk associated with identity lifecycle management, privileged access, excessive or unauthorized access, service and non-human identities, entitlement structures, authentication, access certification, and segregation of duties.

The Director, Strategic Sourcing Indirect will lead sourcing strategy, supplier management, and commercial execution across Software, IT, Professional Services, Marketing and Travel covering approx. $400M of spend and supporting R&D, manufacturing, and commercial functions.

This role is responsible for managing a team of sourcing professionals and leaders and serving as the Business Partner for the IT organization to enable compliant, scalable, and cost-effective procurement of Software licenses, IT services, Infrastructure, and Cloud technologies.

The ideal candidate combines strong people leadership with deep experience in Indirect Sourcing and Procurement, contract negotiation, and brings either domain expertise or education in data science, or advanced analytics within a regulated Life Sciences environment. Subject matter expertise in the IT Procurement space is a plus.

Responsibilities

Leadership & Team Development
· Lead and develop a high-performing sourcing team and leaders supporting Indirect categories
· Set strategic direction, performance goals, and talent development plans
· Ensure diversity of thought and inclusive teamwork with a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement

Category Strategy

Job Description

Interested candidates are invited to visit the Russell Reynolds Engage platform at Engage.RussellReynolds.com . Candidates will be asked to register and create a profile. From the home page, navigate to “Job Post”, click “Apply for Position”, and enter the following career code: 2609-162NA to submit materials for consideration. NOTE: Applying to the MacArthur career site may cause delays in review of your application.

The Opportunity
Philanthropy has long operated with fragmented data, duplicative processes, and systems that do not easily speak to one another. The Philanthropy Data Commons (PDC) was created to change that.

By enabling information to move securely across the systems that organizations already use, the PDC can reduce the repetitive administrative burden on nonprofits, help changemakers gain greater visibility to aligned funders, and give them greater control over how their information is shared, while giving funders a clearer view of organizations, needs, and funding flows.

The PDC has moved well beyond an idea. With significant foundational work completed, including a live Exchange application, an evolving governance framework, a growing network of funders and ecosystem participants, and more than 20 organizations committed to sharing data, PDC is entering an important period of transition and growth.

The focus now is on expanding participation, demonstrating the value of shared data at greater scale, and building the coalition that can make PDC an enduring part of how philanthropy works.

The inaugural Executive Director will have a rare chance to help shape the next stage of the initiative and a broader shift in the field. They will build on significant investment and momentum while helping the PDC grow its reach, deepen its partnerships, strengthen its financial sustainability, and establish its long-term organizational home.

At a time when advances in AI are making access to trusted, well-governed data increasingly important, the PDC has the potential to become essential infrastructure for a more connected, informed, and effective philanthropic sector. For an entrepreneurial leader energized by building in ambiguity, this is a chance to take years of investment and a powerful sector-wide idea and turn it into something enduring, shaping not only the future of the PDC but how philanthropy shares and uses data.

Conceptualized in 2021, the Philanthropy Data Commons is a collaborative initiative temporarily hosted by Mac Services, Inc. that connects the systems, organizations, and data that philanthropy runs on. It provides a shared infrastructure that allows funders, changemakers, and the ecosystem partners they already use to share information on their own terms.

The Vice President, Digital Product Strategy leads Nexstar’s digital product strategy and owns the product initiatives behind two pillars of the 2027 digital strategy: deepening audience relationships and modernizing our platforms. The role turns that work into a sequenced roadmap, clear targets, and shipped products across The Hill, NewsNation, and Nexstar’s local stations, and supports strategic projects, from new business opportunities to partnership and investment evaluations. The VP also plays a critical role in shaping and managing Nexstar’s corporate digital strategy, from annual and quarterly priorities down to product roadmaps.

Two flagship initiatives anchor the role in 2027. The first is Nexstar’s first-party data strategy: growing known, registered users across the portfolio and building the data capture and identity infrastructure behind them. The second is Mobile App 2.0: the redesign, build, and rollout of Nexstar’s station mobile app experience, starting in a lead test market and scaling across the station footprint.

The VP holds direct ownership and day-to-day decision authority over the initiatives, roadmaps, and team she leads, and is accountable for keeping editorial, marketing, revenue, and product aligned behind them.
Success in this role will require strong matrix leadership: the ability to build trusted relationships, create alignment, and form durable alliances across teams whose resources do not directly report into the role. The VP will need to influence and marshal shared engineering, design, product, editorial, marketing, revenue, and station leadership capacity behind the highest-priority initiatives, ensuring that complex cross-functional work moves from strategy to execution with clear ownership and momentum.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

2027 Priorities

• First-Party Data (Deepen Audience Relationships): Owns first-party data strategy across the portfolio, including free account registration, profile data collection, identity resolution, and known-user growth. Sets and owns known-user targets, and defines the roadmap for data capture and identity infrastructure that underpins marketing, advertising, and subscription use cases.
• Mobile App 2.0 (Modernize Our Platforms): Leads the design, development, and rollout of the next-generation Nexstar station mobile app, from a lead test market to the full station footprint.
Owns the product vision, vendor and partner management, launch sequencing, and adoption and engagement targets, and makes the app a primary engine for registration and first-party data.
• OVP Upgrade (Modernize Our Platforms): Supports, but does not own, the upgrade of Nexstar’s online video platform (OVP), the other major platform modernization effort in 2027. Contributes product input where it intersects with Mobile App 2.0 and first-party data.
• CTV (Modernize Our Platforms): Helps drive the enhancement of Nexstar’s connected TV (CTV) presence, improving the viewer experience across Nexstar’s CTV apps

Summary:
The Center for Research Innovation (CRI) at Northeastern University is seeking a dynamic and entrepreneurial Director of Technology Ventures to lead the development and acceleration of Northeastern's spinout portfolio. This role carries two closely linked mandates. First, the Director will directly oversee a portfolio of life sciences and physical sciences spinouts, working hands-on with founding teams to sharpen product-market fit, define go-to-market strategy, and move ventures from formation through launch. Make an impact at NTT Global Data Centers
Join NTT Global Data Centers and be part of a team that drives innovation and sustainability in the digital world. With over 150 data centers across more than 20 countries globally, we offer unparalleled opportunities to work on cutting-edge technology and transformative projects. Experience a collaborative, innovative, and inclusive workplace where your ideas are valued, and your growth is supported.

Your role at a glance
The Director, Engineering Standards and Safety is a global role, that leads the global function that defines how engineering work is performed safely and consistently across data center operations. The role owns engineering standards, technical methods, operating boundaries, asset-acceptance criteria and the governance of technical deviations and risk acceptances. This director leads a multidisciplinary team covering electrical, mechanical, controls, fire and life safety, and related engineering disciplines. The discipline standards engineers carry the primary research, evidence development, consultation and drafting workload. The Director sets priorities, challenges the evidence and retains final approval and governance authority. The function works with Field Engineering, Operations, Design, Construction, Commissioning, vendors and corporate safety teams to convert technical risk and operating experience into practical global requirements. Regional teams remain accountable for executing engineering work. Clear standards and safety controls help operating teams run critical facilities safely and efficiently, maintain reliable infrastructure, reduce avoidable environmental impact and provide consistent technical support to clients.
What we are looking for
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Set the global strategy, priorities and operating model for Engineering Standards & Safety.
- Set the standards-development portfolio and research priorities, assign accountable discipline engineers and ensure work is proportionate to risk and business need.
- Review and approve engineering standards, technical methods and analytical models developed through documented research and cross-functional consultation.
- Ensure discipline engineers engage Field Engineering, site Operations, vendors and other experts, reconcile material input and maintain a traceable technical basis for each recommendation.
- Define technical operating limits, system boundaries and escalation requirements for electrical, mechanical, controls, fire and life-safety systems.
- Establish engineering acceptance criteria for assets and systems entering operation, in partnership with Design, Construction, Commissioning and Operations.
- Define validation frameworks for reliability analysis, energy analysis, technical-capacity analysis and control-strategy design.
- Own the governance process for technical deviations and engineering risk acceptances, including approval authorities, evidence requirements, review periods and escalation thresholds

The Company

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards.  Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day.  We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.

Want to help pets live their best lives?

We’re proud to be where the pets go and where the  pet people  go. If you want to make a real difference, create an exciting career path, feel welcome to be your whole self and nurture your wellbeing,  Petco is the place for you .

Our core values capture that spirit as we work to improve lives by doing what’s right for pets and people.
- Pet First – Protect & Empower.  All pets should  Live their Best Life.  We put the needs of pets and pet parents at the center of everything we do.
- Foster the Fun – Connect & Bond.  Our  Passion  for pets brings us together! We celebrate the journey of pet parenthood through distinct experiences, products, and services.
- Let’s Go! Own & Commit.  We are stronger as  One Petco team.  We bring our unique superpowers and champion authenticity in everyone to drive success.

About Petco:

We’re proud to be  "where the pets go"  to find everything they need to live their best lives for more than 60 years — from their favorite meals and toys, to trusted supplies and expert support from people who get it, because we live it. We believe in the universal truths of pet parenthood — the boundless boops, missing slippers, late night zoomies and everything in between. And we’re here for it. Every tail wag, every vet visit, every step of the way. We are  29,000+  strong and together we nurture the pet-human bond in more than  1,500  Petco stores across the U.S., Mexico and Puerto Rico,  250+  Vetco Total Care hospitals, hundreds of preventive care clinics and eight distribution centers. In 1999, we founded  Petco Love . Together, we support thousands of local animal welfare groups nationwide and have helped find homes for approximately  7 million animals  through in-store adoption events.

They serve as the enterprise owner of the digital P&L, championing customer-first experiences, operational excellence, merchandising rigor, and technology-enabled innovation.

Key Responsibilities
Digital Commerce Leadership & P&L Ownership
- Own the full digital P&L, including revenue, margin, conversion, AOV, and profitability targets across sites, mobile web, and app
- Develop and execute the annual digital commerce strategy, aligning across Merch, Marketing, Supply Chain, Finance, and Technology.
- Drive demand forecasting, digital promotions, price strategy inputs, and forecasting alignment with Planning, FP&A, and Merchandising
- Identify and scale emerging digital growth opportunities, including new categories, business models, and innovative commerce

At Pfizer, our business development and strategic planning teams serve as the corporate face in crucial negotiations that influence our capacity to deliver life-changing breakthroughs for patients. Deep technical understanding of how LLMs, agents, and modern product stacks behave anchors the role’s credibility with Engineering and Product.

Location
This role can be based in Boston, MA or Santa Barbara, CA.

The Role
Sonos is hiring a Vice President of Enterprise Acceleration to lead our global enterprise technology organization at a pivotal moment. Who we are looking for
The Head of Enterprise Architecture owns the target-state design of the technology estate and the standards, patterns and governance through which it is realised . This is the architectural blueprint that determines how every platform, application and integration in the firm is built, connected, secured and retired.

The mandate is to reduce complexity while increasing optionality — cutting technical debt, rationalising a fragmented estate, and establishing the reusable architectural foundations that let engineering teams move faster within known-good boundaries. Success is measured not in documents published but in estate outcomes: fewer bespoke solutions, faster architectural decisions, demonstrably lower run cost, and an architecture capable of absorbing the pace of change that Frontier AI and post-quantum cryptography will impose.

A central element of this mandate is establishing the architecture that makes the firm AI-forward — the compute, serving, integration and control foundations on which AI becomes a governed production capability rather than a portfolio of experiments. This is delivered in deliberate partnership with the Head of Data & AI, who owns model strategy, data products and AI delivery.

This is a deeply technical leadership role . The successful candidate is a credible principal-level architect who has personally designed systems at scale, and who will lead through technical authority rather than positional mandate — equally effective authoring a reference architecture, defending a standard to a skeptical business-unit CIO, and presenting an estate rationalization case to the Senior Leadership.

Why this role is Important to us
- Architecture is an enabling layer, not a gate. Governance exists to accelerate good decisions, not to inspect bad ones after the fact. If review is the bottleneck, the pattern library has failed.
- Patterns over permissions. The fastest, cheapest, pre-approved way to build is to use an existing pattern. Teams may deviate through a time-boxed, registered exception — and inherit the support and compliance burden of doing so.
- Reduce before you add. Every new pattern admitted to the library should retire something. Complexity is the primary long-term cost driver of the estate.
- Serve the whole estate. Mainframe, vendor-package, analytics and quant populations receive proportionate patterns and standards. An architecture that governs only greenfield services has failed.
- Cost is an architectural property. Spend, unit economics and run cost are designed in, not discovered in the invoice — including the economics of accelerated compute and inference.
- Complementary, not overlapping. Where a peer function owns a domain — Data & AI, Cyber, Developer Platforms — EA owns the interfaces, standards and cross-domain coherence, not the delivery.

Architecture strategy & governance

Ready for a challenge?

Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.

Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.

About this role

Our logistics network spans 16 markets, hundreds of thousands of couriers and more than 350 million orders a year. Behind every order are real-time decisions: who delivers it, when, and at what price. Models running in production make them.

We are looking for a Director of Data Science & Machine Learning to lead the function behind those decisions and take the optimisation of our network to the next level. This is a leader-of-leaders role: a global team of 90+ data scientists, operations research scientists, ML engineers and MLOps engineers, led through managers and principal data scientists. You will set the DS/OR/ML agenda, not just run it.

The challenge is dual: keeping the real-time decision systems reliable at marketplace scale, while pushing the frontier on optimisation, supply/demand shaping and applied AI.

Location: Hybrid, 3 days a week from our London or Amsterdam office and 2 days working from home

- Deliver measurable improvement in delivery time, courier utilisation, cost per order, and the efficiency of courier pay.
- Own the strategy and roadmap for real-time decision systems: demand forecasting and supply balancing, order-to-courier assignment, and dynamic pay and fee pricing. All running as low latency production services at marketplace scale.
- Understand and shape courier behaviour: lead incentive and pay design grounded in economics and causal modelling, anticipating how couriers respond to the levers we pull
- Set the Operations Research agenda: combinatorial optimisation, exact and heuristic solvers, and simulation for capacity planning and policy testing

- Build applied AI that delivers value in production, including LLM-based and agentic products for couriers and operations
- Build the organisation: hire, develop managers and principals, and build university partnerships

As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway— you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.

POSITION SUMMARY
The Vice President, Business Transformation will accelerate performance across Marmon Retail by helping its businesses adopt and fully leverage the capabilities, practices, and expertise available across Marmon.

This leader will serve as a strategic partner to company presidents and leadership teams, translating enterprise resources into practical solutions that advance each business's strategic priorities. The role will work closely with Marmon Centers of Excellence (COEs), including Strategy and Marketing Management (SMM), Lean, 80/20, Information Technology, and Innovation, to embed proven practices and build sustainable capability within the businesses.

Success will be measured by stronger business capability, disciplined execution, adoption of proven practices, and measurable improvement in business outcomes. The role is not intended to build a large, centralized function or add layers of resources. Instead, it will connect Marmon expertise with business needs, facilitate implementation, and strengthen ownership within each operating company.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Enterprise Capability Deployment
- Partner with company presidents and leadership teams to identify the highest-value opportunities for Marmon capabilities to improve business performance.
